steps: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and zests, add the milk, eggs and orange blossom water and knead 10 minutes, then knead in the butter until smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 1½ to 2 hours until doubled.
Shape into a ball, poke a hole in the centre and stretch into a large ring on a lined tray; hide a small wrapped figurine and a dried bean underneath if you like.
Prove for 1 hour until puffy, brush with egg and decorate with candied fruit, almonds and sugar.
Bake at 180 °C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden, cool, and optionally split and fill with whipped cream; serve on 6 January with hot chocolate.

ingredients: 750 ml bottle of Spanish red wine (such as Rioja or Tempranillo), bought from a licensed producer
60 ml brandy (brandy de Jerez) or orange liqueur
300 ml soda water or lemonade, chilled
steps: Put the fruit, sugar and cinnamon in a large jug, pour over the brandy and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the wine, stir, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours so the fruit flavours the wine.
Just before serving add the chilled soda water and plenty of ice, and pour into glasses with some fruit; serve to adults only.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml young red wine, bought from a licensed producer
500 ml lemon soda (gaseosa de limón) or lemonade, chilled
steps: Fill tall glasses with ice and a slice of lemon.
Pour in red wine and lemon soda in equal parts, stir gently and serve immediately as a summer drink for adults.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 25 ml Spanish brandy, rum or orujo, bought from a licensed producer
a strip of lemon peel and a few coffee beans, optional
steps: Brew a short, strong espresso.
Warm the brandy in a small glass with the sugar, lemon peel and coffee beans if using.
Pour the hot espresso over the brandy, stir and serve immediately as an after-meal drink for adults.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg very ripe tomatoes, cored and quartered
1 green Italian pepper (pimiento italiano), seeded and chopped
60 g day-old white bread, soaked in water
100 ml Andalusian extra-virgin olive oil (Picual or Hojiblanca)
2 tbsp sherry vinegar (vinagre de Jerez), or red wine vinegar
steps: Blend the tomatoes, pepper, cucumber, garlic and squeezed-out bread on high for 2 minutes until completely smooth.
With the blender running, pour in the olive oil in a thin stream so the soup turns pale orange and emulsified, then add the vinegar and salt.
Thin with cold water to a drinkable consistency and pass through a fine sieve for a silky texture.
Chill for at least 2 hours, then serve very cold in glasses or bowls with small dice of cucumber, pepper and fried bread croutons on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g day-old dense white bread (pan de telera), crusts removed
60 g jamón serrano or ibérico, finely diced
steps: Blend the tomatoes until liquid and strain through a sieve to remove skins and seeds.
Tear the bread into the tomato liquid, add the garlic and salt, soak for 10 minutes, then blend for 2 minutes until thick and smooth.
With the motor running, drizzle in the olive oil until the cream is thick, glossy and coats a spoon; add the vinegar if using and chill for 2 hours.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until fully hard, cool in cold water, peel and chop finely.
Serve cold in shallow bowls topped with chopped egg, diced jamón and a thread of olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g blanched raw almonds (almendras marconas if possible)
100 g day-old white bread, crusts removed and soaked in water
2 garlic cloves, peeled and germ removed
200 g green Muscatel grapes (uvas moscatel), peeled and halved
steps: Blend the almonds and garlic with a splash of the water until a fine paste forms.
Add the squeezed bread, salt and vinegar, then blend while slowly adding the olive oil until creamy and white.
Add the remaining ice-cold water and blend for 2 minutes; strain through a fine sieve for a smooth finish.
Chill for 2 hours and serve very cold, garnished with peeled grapes (or diced melon or apple) and a drizzle of oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g day-old white bread, crusts removed
1 can (120 g) tuna in olive oil, drained
steps: Blend the tomatoes, pepper and garlic until liquid, then add the torn bread and let it soak for 10 minutes.
Blend again while drizzling in the oil until very thick, thicker than salmorejo, then season with vinegar and salt and chill for 2 hours.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until fully hard, cool, peel and chop.
Serve the cold porra in a wide earthenware dish topped with chopped egg, jamón and flaked tuna, with extra bread for scooping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
300 g white fish fillet such as hake (merluza), cut into pieces
200 ml mild olive oil or sunflower oil
steps: Simmer the potatoes in the fish stock over medium heat for 15 minutes until just tender.
Add the fish and prawns and poach for 5 minutes until the fish flakes and the prawns are pink and cooked through; remove from heat.
Meanwhile whisk the yolks with salt and lemon juice and slowly add the oil to make a thick homemade mayonnaise.
Temper the mayonnaise by whisking in a ladle of hot stock at a time until you have added about half the stock, then pour it back into the pot.
Warm gently over low heat for 2 minutes, stirring and never boiling so it does not split; season with vinegar and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 litres chicken and ham stock (caldo de puchero)
60 g thin noodles (fideos finos) or rice
steps: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until fully hard, cool, peel and chop finely.
Bring the stock to a boil, add the noodles and cook for 5 minutes until tender (15 minutes if using rice).
Stir in the diced jamón and fino sherry and simmer for 2 minutes; check salt, as ham adds plenty.
Ladle into bowls, scatter over the chopped egg and a few mint leaves, and serve piping hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Put the beef, chicken, tocino and ham bone in a large pot with the cold water, bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Add the drained chickpeas in a net or loose, then the carrots, leek and celery; simmer gently, covered, for 2.5 hours until the beef is tender.
Add the potatoes and cook for 25 more minutes until soft; season with salt.
Strain off the broth to serve first as soup (or to make sopa de picadillo), then serve the chickpeas, vegetables and meats as a second course; leftover meat becomes pringá.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g dried white beans (alubias), soaked overnight
500 g green chard or green beans, chopped
2 garlic cloves and 1 tsp sweet pimentón
steps: Cover the chickpeas, beans, pork belly and ribs with cold water, bring to a boil, skim and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add the chard or green beans, chorizo and morcilla and simmer for 40 more minutes until the legumes are creamy and all meat is fully cooked.
Fry the sliced garlic in oil until golden, take off heat, stir in the pimentón and a ladle of broth, then pour this sofrito into the pot.
Simmer for 5 minutes, season and rest briefly; serve hot with the meats (the pringá) on the side and bread.

ingredients: 300 g hake or cod fillet, cut into strips
200 g chickpea-wheat frying flour (harina de freír), or plain flour
steps: Pat all the fish completely dry and season lightly with salt.
Heat the olive oil in a deep pan to 180°C, until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds.
Toss the fish in flour, shake off the excess in a sieve so only a fine coating remains.
Fry in small batches for 2-3 minutes until crisp, golden and the flesh is opaque and cooked through; drain on paper.
Serve immediately in a paper cone or on a platter with lemon wedges and a cold drink.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g fresh anchovies (boquerones), heads and guts removed
150 g frying flour (harina de freír) or plain flour
steps: Rinse and dry the anchovies well; press them together by the tails in fans of 4-5 (en abanico) if you like.
Heat the oil to 180°C in a deep frying pan.
Salt the fish, dredge in flour and shake off the excess.
Fry for 2 minutes until crisp and golden and the fish is cooked through, drain on paper and serve hot with lemon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g tiny live or fresh shrimp (camarones), or the smallest brown shrimp you can find
steps: Whisk both flours with salt and cold water into a thin batter like single cream, then rest in the fridge for 1 hour.
Stir in the onion, parsley and whole shrimp.
Heat 1 cm of olive oil in a frying pan over high heat until shimmering (about 190°C).
Spoon in thin ladles of batter, spreading to lacy discs; fry 1-2 minutes per side until very crisp and golden and the shrimp are cooked.
Drain on paper and serve at once, ideally with a glass of chilled manzanilla.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g dogfish or tope shark (cazón), skinned and cut into 3 cm cubes; substitute monkfish
150 g frying flour or chickpea flour
steps: Mix garlic, pimentón, cumin, oregano, vinegar, water and salt to make the adobo.
Toss the fish in the adobo, cover and marinate in the fridge overnight (8 hours or more).
Drain well, pat dry and coat in flour, shaking off the excess.
Fry in 180°C olive oil in batches for 3-4 minutes until deep golden and cooked through; drain and serve hot with lemon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g cuttlefish (chocos), cleaned and cut into finger-thick strips; substitute squid
150 g frying flour or plain flour
steps: Dry the cuttlefish strips thoroughly and season with salt.
Heat the oil to 180°C in a deep pan.
Coat in flour, shake off the excess and fry in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and just tender.
Drain on paper and serve immediately with lemon, Huelva style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rinse the baby squid, drain and dry very well on a towel.
Heat the oil to 190°C.
Season, toss in flour and shake hard in a sieve to remove the excess.
Fry in small batches for 1-2 minutes until crisp and golden, drain and serve hot with lemon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g sea anemones (ortiguillas), cleaned; substitute large oysters or mussels, shucked
150 g frying flour or chickpea flour
steps: Wearing gloves, rinse the anemones several times in salted water to remove sand, then drain thoroughly.
Heat the olive oil to 180°C.
Dredge the anemones in flour, shake off excess and fry in batches for 3 minutes until crisp outside and set inside.
Drain on paper, salt lightly and serve at once with lemon, as in Cádiz bars.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg live coquinas (wedge clams), or small clams
steps: Soak the coquinas in cold salted water for 2 hours, changing the water twice, to purge sand; discard any open ones that do not close when tapped.
Gently fry the garlic and chilli in the oil over medium heat for 1 minute until just golden.
Add the clams and sherry, cover and cook over high heat for 2-3 minutes, shaking the pan, until all shells open; discard any that stay closed.
Scatter with parsley and serve immediately with bread to mop the juices.

ingredients: 1 kg small live snails (caracoles chicos), purged
2 tbsp mixed snail spices (hierbabuena, poleo/pennyroyal, fennel seed, cumin, cayenne, black peppercorns)
steps: Wash the snails repeatedly in cold water with a handful of salt, rinsing until the water runs clear.
Put them in a pot of cold water and heat very slowly so they come out of their shells, then raise to a boil and skim for 5 minutes; drain and refill with fresh water.
Add the onion, garlic, pepper, spices tied in a muslin, pimentón, bay leaf and salt.
Simmer gently for 1 hour until the snails are tender and the broth is aromatic.
Serve hot in small bowls with plenty of the caldo, eaten with toothpicks, as is typical in Seville in May.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg large snails (cabrillas), purged and cleaned
steps: Wash the snails in several changes of salted water, then blanch in boiling water for 10 minutes and drain.
Fry onion and garlic in olive oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, pimentón, cayenne, cumin and bay leaf and cook for 10 minutes into a thick spicy sauce.
Add the snails and 500 ml water, then simmer for 40 minutes until tender and the sauce coats them; season and serve hot with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 16 large fresh sardines, whole and ungutted (traditional) or gutted
steps: Rinse the sardines and skewer 4 per skewer through the backbone area, so they sit side by side.
Sprinkle generously with coarse salt.
Grill over a wood fire or very hot charcoal, angled toward the heat, for 4-5 minutes per side until the skin blisters and the flesh is opaque to the bone.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve hot with lemon, as on the beaches of Málaga.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g fresh bluefin tuna (atún de almadraba) steak, cut into large cubes
150 ml fino sherry or dry white wine
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Season the tuna and sear it in a little oil over high heat for 1 minute per side; set aside.
In the same pan cook the onions, garlic and bay in the remaining oil over low heat for 25 minutes until very soft and golden.
Stir in the pimentón, add the sherry and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Return the tuna, cover and cook gently for 5-6 minutes until cooked through but still juicy; serve hot with fried potatoes or bread.

ingredients: 1.2 kg urta (red-banded seabream) in thick slices; substitute sea bream or snapper
1 green pepper and 1 red pepper, cut into strips
150 ml fino sherry or dry white wine
steps: Sauté the onion, peppers and garlic in olive oil over medium heat for 12 minutes until soft.
Add the grated tomato, bay and thyme and cook for 10 minutes until jammy.
Pour in the sherry, simmer for 3 minutes, then lay in the salted fish slices.
Cover and cook gently for 10-12 minutes, spooning sauce over, until the fish flakes easily; serve hot with fried potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp sweet smoked pimentón (pimentón de la Vera)
steps: Wilt the spinach in a large pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, then drain and chop.
Fry the garlic and bread in the olive oil until golden, then pound in a mortar with the cumin, pimentón and vinegar to a thick paste.
Return the spinach to the pan with the chickpeas, stir in the paste and 150 ml water.
Simmer for 10 minutes until thick and fragrant; season and serve warm as a Sevillian tapa with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg oxtail (rabo de toro), cut at the joints
500 ml red wine (from Montilla-Moriles or Rioja)
500 ml beef stock and 1 tsp salt
steps: Season and flour the oxtail, then brown it well in olive oil in a heavy pot over high heat; set aside.
Cook the onions, carrots, pepper and garlic in the same pot for 15 minutes until soft and caramelised.
Return the meat, add the wine and boil for 5 minutes, then add stock, bay and cloves.
Cover and simmer very gently for 3 hours until the meat falls from the bone.
Lift out the meat, blend or sieve the sauce until smooth, reduce if thin, and serve the oxtail coated in sauce with fried potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 thin pork loin fillets (lomo), pounded very thin
steps: Overlap 2 pork fillets on a board, lay 2 slices of jamón on top and roll up tightly into a long log; repeat for 4 rolls.
Season lightly, then coat each roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs, pressing firmly.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry the rolls for 6-8 minutes, turning, until deep golden and the pork reaches 71°C inside.
Drain and serve hot, cut in half, with fried potatoes and mayonnaise or salmorejo.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 roasted red pepper (pimiento morrón), cut into strips
3 tbsp olive oil and 1 tsp salt
steps: Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil for 8 minutes, add chorizo and jamón and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes into a thick sauce; stir in the peas.
Divide the sauce among 4 earthenware dishes (cazuelas), crack 2 eggs into each and arrange pepper strips and asparagus around them.
Bake at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until the whites are fully set and the yolks are as firm as you like; serve hot with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g cooked meats from a puchero (beef, chicken, tocino)
steps: Remove any bones and skin from the cooked meats and put everything on a board.
Chop and mash the meats, tocino, morcilla and chorizo together with a knife or fork into a coarse, unctuous paste.
Warm it in a pan with the olive oil for 5 minutes until hot through.
Pile into split, lightly toasted bread rolls (montaditos de pringá) and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 ml Pedro Ximénez sherry or oloroso
steps: Season the cheeks and brown them in olive oil over high heat in a heavy casserole; set aside.
Add onions, carrots and garlic and cook for 15 minutes until golden.
Return the cheeks, pour in the sherry and wine, boil for 5 minutes, then add stock, bay and thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours until the cheeks yield to a spoon.
Blend the sauce smooth, reduce until glossy, and serve the cheeks in sauce with mashed or fried potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g pork tenderloin (solomillo de cerdo), cut into 2 cm medallions
1 whole head garlic, cloves peeled and lightly crushed
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Gently fry the garlic in olive oil over low heat for 8 minutes until golden and soft; remove and keep.
Season the medallions and sear in the same oil over high heat for 2 minutes per side.
Off the heat pour in the whisky, then return to heat and let it bubble for 2 minutes (it may flame, so keep a lid nearby).
Add stock, lemon juice and the garlic, simmer for 4-5 minutes until the pork is cooked through (71°C) and the sauce is reduced; serve with fried potatoes, Seville style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g lamb or veal kidneys, cleaned and sliced
2 tbsp white wine vinegar for soaking
150 ml dry oloroso or fino sherry
steps: Remove the white core from the kidneys, slice, and soak in cold water with the vinegar for 1 hour; rinse and dry.
Sear the kidneys in hot oil for 2 minutes over high heat, then drain off the bitter liquid they release.
In fresh oil, fry the onion and garlic for 6 minutes, stir in the flour, then add the sherry and stock to make a sauce.
Return the kidneys and simmer 3-4 minutes until just cooked through with no pink juices; sprinkle with parsley and serve with bread or rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg young kid goat (choto), chopped into pieces; substitute lamb
1 whole head garlic, cloves unpeeled and crushed
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Season the meat and brown it in olive oil over medium-high heat for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic cloves and bay leaves and fry for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the pimentón and thyme, then add the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Cover and cook gently for 30-35 minutes until the meat is tender and the juices are reduced; serve with fried potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g lamb brains and/or veal sweetbreads (sesos y criadillas), cleaned; substitute chicken livers
steps: Blanch the brains or sweetbreads in simmering salted water for 10 minutes until firm, cool and dice.
Fry the onion in olive oil for 6 minutes, then add jamón, offal and peas and cook 4 minutes.
Beat the eggs with salt, stir in the filling and the red pepper.
Pour into a hot oiled pan, cook over medium heat for 4 minutes, flip with a plate and cook 3 more minutes until fully set; serve warm, as in Granada's Sacromonte.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g flour and 100 ml water with a pinch of saffron for the gurullos (or orzo-size pasta)
steps: Knead flour, saffron water and a pinch of salt into a firm dough, roll pieces into tiny grain-shaped gurullos and let them dry for 20 minutes.
Brown the seasoned rabbit in olive oil, then add onion, pepper and garlic and cook 10 minutes.
Add tomato and pimentón, cook 5 minutes, pour in the water and simmer for 40 minutes until the rabbit is tender.
Add the gurullos and cook for 12-15 minutes until tender and the stew is thick; rest 5 minutes and serve hot, Almería style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g plain flour, 130 ml water and a pinch of salt for the andrajos
1/2 rabbit or 300 g hare, cut in pieces
200 g cod or salt cod, desalted (optional, Jaén style)
1 tsp sweet pimentón and 1 bay leaf
steps: Knead flour, water and salt into a smooth dough, roll thin and tear into rough rags (andrajos).
Brown the seasoned rabbit in olive oil, add onion, pepper and garlic and cook 10 minutes.
Add tomato, pimentón and bay, cook 5 minutes, then the water, and simmer for 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the cod if using, then the dough rags, and cook 10 minutes until the pasta is tender and the broth thickened; serve hot in bowls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg fresh young broad beans (habas), shelled, or 500 g frozen
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the jamón and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the broad beans and wine, cover and cook gently for 12-15 minutes until tender, adding a splash of water if dry.
Season, taking care with salt, and serve warm, as in Granada.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
1 green Italian pepper, cut into strips
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add potatoes, onion, peppers and garlic, season with salt and stir to coat.
Cook slowly for 30-35 minutes, turning occasionally, until the potatoes are soft and some edges are golden; they should poach rather than crisp.
Drain off excess oil (keep it for cooking) and serve hot as a side to meat, fish or eggs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp ground cumin and 1 tsp sweet pimentón
steps: Salt the aubergine cubes for 15 minutes, rinse and pat dry.
Fry the onion, garlic and peppers in olive oil over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the aubergine, pumpkin and courgette and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tomato, cumin and pimentón and simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the stew is thick; serve warm or at room temperature with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 small spring onion or sweet onion (cebolleta), finely sliced
steps: Boil the potatoes whole in salted water for 20-25 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain, cool slightly, peel and cut into thick slices or chunks.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar and salt, and pour over the warm potatoes with the onion and parsley.
Toss gently and rest for 30 minutes so the potatoes absorb the dressing; serve at room temperature, Cádiz style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 can (120 g) tuna in olive oil, drained
steps: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until fully hard, cool, peel and chop.
Combine the tomato, pepper, cucumber and onion in a bowl.
Dress with olive oil, vinegar and salt, then fold in the tuna and egg.
Chill for 30 minutes and serve cold with bread to soak up the juices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g salt cod (bacalao), desalted and flaked, or grilled cod
steps: Use salt cod that has been desalted in cold water for 48 hours with several changes, or flake cooked cod; pat it dry.
Arrange the orange slices on a platter and scatter over the cod, onion and olives.
Add the quartered hard-boiled eggs.
Dress with olive oil and a little salt and serve cool.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g salt cod, desalted and flaked, or cooked cod
2 oranges, peeled and cut into segments
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20-25 minutes until tender, then cool, peel and slice.
If using desalted raw cod, poach it for 3 minutes until opaque and flake it.
Combine potatoes, cod, orange, onion and olives in a bowl.
Dress with olive oil, vinegar and salt, toss gently and serve at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g fresh yeast or 4 g dried yeast
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water, mix with flour, salt and oil and knead 10 minutes into a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and let rise for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide into 8, shape into flat ovals, dust heavily with flour and let rise 45 minutes.
Bake at 240°C for 12-15 minutes until pale and soft with no colour on top; cool under a cloth and serve split and toasted with olive oil and tomato.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g pork loin (lomo), finely diced or shredded
1/2 tsp ground cumin and 1/2 tsp dried oregano
steps: Fry the pork pieces with garlic in 2 tbsp lard over medium heat for 10 minutes until fully cooked.
Add the remaining lard and melt over low heat, then stir in the bay leaf, oregano, cumin and salt.
Take off the heat and stir in both pimentones so they do not burn; cool until set to a soft orange spread (manteca colorá).
Split and toast the molletes, spread with the warm or room-temperature manteca including the meat and serve for breakfast with coffee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 ml extra-virgin olive oil, plus 1 litre for frying
1 tbsp aniseed (matalahúva) and 1 tbsp sesame seeds
steps: Fry the orange peel in 150 ml olive oil until dark, discard it, then add the aniseed and sesame off the heat and let cool slightly.
Mix the flavoured oil with the flour, wine and salt and knead into a smooth, elastic dough; rest 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thin, cut into 8 cm squares and fold two opposite corners over each other, pressing to seal.
Fry in 175°C olive oil for 2-3 minutes until golden and blistered; drain.
Warm the honey with water, dip each pestiño and let drain on a rack; serve at Christmas or Holy Week.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp aniseed (matalahúva) and 1 tbsp sesame seeds
steps: Warm the oil with the aniseed and sesame until fragrant, then cool to lukewarm.
Mix flour, yeast, salt, water and the oil into a smooth dough, then let rise 1 hour.
Divide into 8 balls and roll paper-thin into 14 cm rounds on baking paper; sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until crisp and golden with caramelised spots; cool on a rack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 125 g Ibérico pork lard (manteca ibérica), soft
60 g almonds, toasted and finely ground
steps: Toast the flour on a tray at 160°C for 20-25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until pale beige; cool completely and sift.
Beat the lard with the icing sugar until creamy, then add flour, almonds, cinnamon, sesame and salt and work into a crumbly dough.
Roll 1.5 cm thick, cut into small ovals and place on a lined tray.
Bake at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until barely coloured, cool fully on the tray as they are very fragile, then dust with icing sugar and wrap in tissue paper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 125 g pork lard (manteca de cerdo), soft
steps: Toast the flour at 160°C for 20 minutes, stirring often, until lightly golden; cool and sift.
Cream the lard with the icing sugar, cinnamon and lemon zest.
Add flour, sesame and salt and press together into a dough; roll 1.5 cm thick and cut into rounds.
Bake at 180°C for 12 minutes until lightly golden, cool completely on the tray and dust with icing sugar.

4 very ripe hanging tomatoes (tomàquets de penjar), or ripe plum tomatoes

2 medium courgettes, cut into 2 cm cubes

200 g salt cod, desalted 24 hours and shredded
150 g good tinned tuna in olive oil, drained

steps: Soak the ñoras in hot water for 20 minutes, then scrape out the flesh; roast the head of garlic at 200 °C for 20 minutes until soft.

ingredients: 24 calçots (sweet Catalan spring onions), or thick spring onions / baby leeks
steps: Trim the roots and the very top of the green leaves; rinse off any soil.

ingredients: 1 botifarra blanca and 1 botifarra negra (Catalan sausages), or mild pork sausages
For the pilota: 250 g minced pork, 1 egg, 2 tbsp breadcrumbs, 1 clove garlic chopped, 1 tbsp parsley, 1/2 tsp salt
2 carrots, 1 leek, 1 celery stick, 1 small turnip
steps: Put beef, chicken, trotter and 3.5 litres cold water in a large pot, bring to the boil, skim the foam and add the soaked chickpeas in a net bag; simmer gently for 2 hours.

ingredients: 1 kg mixed firm white fish (monkfish, hake, scorpion fish/rascassa), cut into chunks
500 g potatoes, cut into thick slices
For the picada: 2 cloves garlic, 20 toasted almonds, 1 slice fried bread, 2 tbsp parsley, 3 saffron threads

steps: Season the chicken with salt and brown it in hot oil in a cassola over medium-high heat for 10 minutes; sear the prawns 1 minute per side and set them aside.

6 small firm pears (ideally Ercolini), peeled with stalks on

2 red bell peppers and 2 aubergines, roasted and peeled into strips (escalivada)
8 anchovy fillets in oil, or 2 botifarres, sliced

ingredients: 2 eggs, beaten, plus 100 g plain flour and 120 g breadcrumbs for coating
Olive or sunflower oil, for deep-frying
To serve: Allioli and a spicy brava sauce (tomato with chilli and paprika)
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until soft, drain and mash smoothly; season and cool.

ingredients: 150 g sugar, plus 6 tbsp for the top
steps: Heat 850 ml of the milk with the lemon peel and cinnamon until just simmering, then remove from the heat and infuse 15 minutes; strain.

ingredients: 400 g mató (fresh unsalted Catalan cheese), or fresh ricotta or requesón

50 g cocoa powder or desiccated coconut (for variations)

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, milk, eggs, sugar, zests, anise and salt and knead 10 minutes, then knead in the butter until the dough is smooth and elastic; rise covered for 2 hours until doubled.

ingredients: Zest of 1 lemon and 1 tsp ground anise seed
Olive or sunflower oil, for deep-frying
steps: Mix flour, yeast, milk, eggs, sugar, olive oil, zest and anise and knead for 10 minutes to a soft dough; rise covered 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
With oiled hands pinch off walnut-size pieces and form small rings with a hole in the middle (or simply drop in small balls).
Deep-fry at 175 °C for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until puffed and golden all over.
Drain on paper and roll in sugar while warm; they are eaten during Lent.

ingredients: 2 tbsp orange-blossom water and zest of 1 orange
100 g candied fruit and 30 g flaked almonds, 3 tbsp pearl sugar for decoration
steps: Knead flour, yeast, milk, eggs, sugar, orange-blossom water, zest and salt for 10 minutes, then knead in the butter; rise 2 hours until doubled.

Roll the dough into a long rectangle, spread or lay the marzipan along it, roll up and join the ends into a ring; hide a small dried bean and a ceramic king figure (wrapped in foil) inside if following tradition.
Prove on a lined tray for 1 hour, brush with egg and decorate with candied fruit, almonds and pearl sugar.
Bake at 180 °C for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding; serve on 6 January (Reis).

ingredients: 500 g strong flour, 10 g dried yeast, 200 ml warm milk, 2 eggs, 80 g sugar, 80 g butter, 1/2 tsp salt
For the crema: 500 ml milk, 4 egg yolks, 100 g sugar, 40 g cornflour, 1 strip lemon peel
steps: Make a soft dough with the flour, yeast, milk, eggs, sugar, butter, salt and zest; knead 10 minutes and rise 2 hours until doubled.
Make a thick crema pastissera by cooking the milk, yolks, sugar, cornflour and lemon peel over low heat, stirring, for 6 to 8 minutes until very thick; cool completely.
Roll the dough 5 mm thick, cut into 10 x 12 cm rectangles, place a line of crema on each and roll up into fat cylinders, sealing well; prove 45 minutes.
Deep-fry at 170 °C for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden, drain and roll in sugar; this Girona pastry is best eaten the same day.

ingredients: 100 ml syrup (100 g sugar boiled 2 minutes with 100 ml water) for soaking
150 g toasted flaked almonds or chocolate truffle cream for the sides
Chocolate eggs and figures, feathers and chicks to decorate
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar for 8 to 10 minutes until pale and tripled, then fold in the sifted flour and baking powder followed by the butter.
Bake in a 22 cm lined tin at 180 °C for 25 to 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean; cool.
Split into two layers, soak with syrup and sandwich with apricot jam; spread jam around the sides and press on toasted almonds.
Decorate the top with chocolate eggs and figures; godparents traditionally give the mona to their godchildren on Easter Monday.

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C; whisk the egg whites lightly with the icing sugar, then mix in the butter, flour and zest to a smooth thin batter.
Spread teaspoons of batter into very thin 10 cm circles on a lined tray, 3 or 4 at a time.
Bake 4 to 6 minutes until the edges turn golden.
Immediately roll each hot wafer around the handle of a wooden spoon to form a tube, and cool; serve at Christmas with cava or dipped in turrón ice cream.

ingredients: For the crema: 500 ml milk, 4 egg yolks, 100 g sugar, 40 g cornflour, 1 strip lemon peel, 1 cinnamon stick
3 tbsp icing sugar or sugar for caramelising
steps: Make the crema: heat the milk with lemon peel and cinnamon, whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour, combine and cook over low heat, stirring, 6 to 8 minutes until thick; cool.
Whisk the eggs and sugar 8 to 10 minutes until pale and thick, fold in the flour, spread 1 cm thick on a lined 30 x 40 cm tray and bake at 200 °C for 8 to 10 minutes until springy.
Turn onto a sugared cloth, peel off the paper and roll up loosely while warm; cool 10 minutes.
Unroll, spread with the crema, roll up tightly and dust or caramelise the top with sugar; chill 1 hour and slice.

ingredients: 1 bottle Catalan ratafia (licensed producer, e.g. from the Garrotxa or Montseny)
steps: Ratafia is a traditional Catalan herbal liqueur made by macerating green walnuts, herbs and spices in spirit, then ageing it; buy it from licensed producers rather than making it at home.
Serve chilled or at cellar temperature in small glasses after a meal as a digestif (40 to 50 ml per person), optionally over ice with a twist of orange peel.
Drink responsibly; it typically contains 25 to 30% alcohol.

ingredients: 800 g chicken, bone-in, cut into small pieces
400 g rabbit, cut into small pieces (or more chicken)
200 g flat green beans (bajoqueta), cut into 4 cm lengths
150 g garrofó (large white lima beans), fresh or soaked frozen
1 large ripe tomato, grated, skin discarded
1 tsp sweet pimentón (smoked or unsmoked paprika)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a 40 cm paella pan over medium-high heat and brown the salted chicken and rabbit slowly on all sides for 15 minutes until deep golden.

Push the meat to the edges, add the green beans and garrofó to the centre and fry for 3 minutes, then add the grated tomato and cook 3 minutes until jammy; stir in the pimentón for 10 seconds without letting it burn.
Pour in the water, add saffron, bring to a boil and simmer 20 minutes to make the broth; taste and adjust salt so it is slightly over-seasoned.

Scatter the rice evenly across the pan in a cross shape, spread it out with a spoon and do not stir again; boil hard for 8 minutes, then lower to a gentle simmer for 9–10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Lay the rosemary on top for the last 2 minutes, then raise the heat for 1–2 minutes until you hear crackling to form the socarrat crust at the base.
Remove from heat, cover with a clean cloth and rest 5 minutes before serving straight from the pan with lemon wedges if liked.

ingredients: 1 kg small rockfish and fish heads (morralla), cleaned
1 ñora pepper, soaked (or 1 tsp sweet paprika)
steps: Fry the fish, heads, prawn shells, 2 whole garlic cloves and the ñora flesh in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, add the water and simmer 35 minutes, then strain to get about 1.2 l fumet.
In a paella pan heat the remaining oil over medium-high heat and fry the cuttlefish for 5 minutes until golden, then add the minced garlic and tomato and cook 3 minutes.
Add the rice, stir to coat for 1 minute, then pour in 1 l hot fumet with the saffron and salt; boil 8 minutes on high, then simmer 8 minutes without stirring.
Scatter the prawns over the top for the last 4 minutes, rest 5 minutes off the heat and serve with allioli on the side (the rice is eaten "a banda", apart from the fish).

ingredients: 500 g squid or cuttlefish, cleaned and diced
steps: Heat the oil in a paella pan over medium heat and fry the squid for 5 minutes until it releases and re-absorbs its liquid.
Add onion, pepper and garlic and cook gently for 10 minutes until soft, then add the tomato and cook 3 minutes more.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then dissolve the squid ink in the hot stock, pour it in, add the salt and bring to a boil.
Cook 8 minutes on high and 9 minutes on low without stirring until the rice is tender and dry; rest 5 minutes and serve with allioli.

ingredients: 300 g pork ribs, cut in pieces
1 potato, peeled and sliced 1 cm thick
1 l hot meat stock (leftover cocido broth is traditional)
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C; in a wide shallow clay dish (cassola) or frying pan heat the oil over medium-high heat and brown the ribs and panceta for 10 minutes, then the potato slices, tomato halves and garlic head for 5 minutes; set aside.
Fry the morcilla briefly for 1 minute per side and set aside, then add the rice and pimentón to the pan oil and stir 1 minute.
Transfer rice to the cassola, add chickpeas and the meats, arrange potato slices, tomato halves cut-side up, morcillas and the garlic head in the centre.
Pour over the hot stock with saffron, check it is well salted, and bake 20–25 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed; rest 5 minutes before serving.

ingredients: 200 g pork ribs, cut in pieces
2 longanizas (fresh pork sausages), cut in chunks
6 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C; in a deep clay dish or ovenproof pan brown the chicken and ribs in the oil over medium-high heat for 15 minutes, then add longaniza and morcilla for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato, cook 3 minutes, then add the stock and saffron and simmer 20 minutes until the meat is tender.
Stir in the rice and chickpeas, simmer on the stovetop for 12 minutes until most liquid is absorbed.
Pour the beaten eggs evenly over the surface and bake 10–15 minutes until the egg crust is set and golden; rest 5 minutes and serve from the dish.

ingredients: 300 g raw prawns, peeled (shells and heads reserved for stock)
200 g monkfish, cut in small cubes
steps: Fry the prawn heads and shells in 2 tbsp oil for 3 minutes, pressing them, then add to the stock and simmer 10 minutes; strain.
In a paella pan heat the remaining oil over medium-high heat, fry the cuttlefish 5 minutes, then the monkfish 2 minutes, and remove the monkfish.
Add garlic and tomato, cook 3 minutes, stir in pimentón and rice for 1 minute, then add the hot stock, saffron and salt.

Boil 8 minutes, then simmer 8 minutes without stirring, returning the monkfish and adding the peeled prawns for the final 4 minutes; rest 5 minutes and serve — all seafood is peeled so the "señorito" eats without using his fingers.

ingredients: 300 g dried white beans (fesols), soaked overnight
400 g pork trotters and ears, cleaned and cut
2 turnips (naps), peeled and cut into chunks
1 bunch chard stalks (penques), cut into 4 cm pieces
steps: Put drained beans, trotters, ears and pork belly in a large pot with the water, bring to a boil, skim and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the turnips, chard stalks and saffron and simmer 30 minutes until the turnips are soft and the beans are creamy.
Add the morcillas and rice, season with salt and simmer 16–18 minutes until the rice is tender but the dish is still brothy (caldoso).
Rest 3 minutes and serve in deep plates, slicing the meats and morcilla for each portion.

ingredients: 400 g fideuà noodles (short thick pasta tubes, no. 2–4)
steps: Heat the oil in a paella pan over medium-high heat, sear the prawns 1 minute per side and set aside; fry the cuttlefish 5 minutes and monkfish 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and toast them for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until golden.
Add garlic and tomato, cook 2 minutes, stir in the pimentón, then pour in the hot stock with saffron.
Simmer 8–10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed, lay the prawns on top, then either rest 5 minutes or put under a hot grill 2 minutes until the noodle tips curl up; serve with allioli.

ingredients: 1 kg eel (anguila), skinned and cut into 5 cm pieces
4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oil in a clay pot (cassola) over medium heat and fry the sliced garlic and chilli for 1 minute until pale gold.
Remove from heat, stir in both pimentóns for 10 seconds, then immediately add the water and potatoes and bring to a boil.
Pound the whole garlic, almonds and fried bread into a paste (picada) and stir it in; simmer 15 minutes.
Add the eel pieces and salt and simmer 12–15 minutes until the eel is cooked through and the potatoes are soft and thickening the red sauce; serve hot with bread (monkfish can replace eel).

ingredients: 200 g salted tuna belly (tonyina de sorra) or good tinned tuna in oil
steps: If using salted tuna, soak it in cold water for 2 hours, changing the water twice, then flake it.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion, garlic and peppers for 15 minutes until very soft.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and salt and cook 15 minutes until thick and jammy.
Stir in the tuna and pine nuts and cook 5 minutes more; serve warm or cold with crusty bread, as in the Cabanyal fishermen's quarter.

ingredients: 200 g pork belly or jowl, minced
250 g pork caul fat (tela/redaño), soaked in cold water
steps: Mix the minced liver and belly with garlic, parsley, spices and salt and chill 20 minutes.
Spread out the caul fat, cut into 15 cm squares, put 2 tbsp mixture in each and wrap into flat patties.
Grill on a griddle or barbecue brushed with oil over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes per side until well browned and cooked through with no pink in the centre (75°C inside).
Serve hot in a bocadillo or with grilled vegetables, as in La Safor and Gandia.

ingredients: 500 g cooked chicken or pork blood (sang cuita), cut into 2 cm cubes
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over low-medium heat and cook the onions with bay leaf and salt for 20 minutes, stirring, until golden and very soft.
Add the blood cubes and oregano and cook gently for 5–7 minutes, turning carefully, until heated through.
Stir in the pimentón off the heat and serve hot as a tapa with bread.

ingredients: 1.5 kg clóchinas (small Valencian mussels, in season May–August) or other mussels
steps: Scrub the mussels, pull off the beards and discard any that are broken or stay open when tapped.
Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and fry the garlic 1 minute, then add bay, peppercorns, water and the juice of half the lemon.
Add the mussels, cover and steam on high heat for 4–5 minutes, shaking the pot, until the shells open; discard any that stay closed.
Serve immediately with the cooking juices and the remaining lemon in wedges.

Cook 2–3 minutes, shaking, until they open, then add garlic, parsley and the remaining oil and toss 30 seconds; discard any unopened ones.

ingredients: 200 g salt cod (bacalao), desalted for 48 hours with water changes
steps: Roast the peppers in a 200°C oven for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until blistered and soft, then cover 10 minutes and peel.
Tear (esgarrar) the peppers into strips by hand; drain the desalted cod, pat dry and tear into fine flakes.
Layer the peppers and cod on a plate, scatter with sliced garlic and olives and season lightly.
Drizzle with olive oil and leave 30 minutes to marinate before serving with bread.

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C, brush the whole vegetables with a little oil and roast for 40–45 minutes, turning once, until soft and charred (tomatoes come out after 20 minutes).

Arrange on a plate, scatter with garlic and salt and dress generously with olive oil and the roasting juices.
Serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

ingredients: 6 dried red peppers (pimiento seco de Alcoy, or ñoras)
150 g dried salt cod (abadejo or bacalao seco), not soaked
steps: Toast the dried cod directly over a flame or on a dry griddle for 2–3 minutes per side until fragrant, then tear it into thin threads.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over low heat and fry the whole garlic cloves for 6–8 minutes until golden; remove.
Fry the dried peppers in the same oil for 20–30 seconds until they darken slightly (do not burn), drain and crumble them into pieces.
Mix peppers, cod and garlic in a bowl, pour over the warm oil and leave 1 hour before serving with bread, as in Alcoy.

ingredients: 250 g dried red or pinto beans (judías pintas), soaked overnight
80 g rice or wheat berries (blat picat)
steps: Simmer the soaked beans, ribs and tocino in the water for 1 hour 30 minutes, skimming.
Add lentils, potato, sweet potato, chard and pimentón and cook 25 minutes.
Add morcillas and rice and season with salt; simmer 15–18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest 5 minutes and serve in bowls with the meats sliced.

ingredients: 500 g beef shank or chicken thighs
2 potatoes, 2 carrots and 1 turnip, peeled and chunked
steps: Simmer the chickpeas, beef and pork belly in the water for 2 hours, skimming foam.
Mix the minced pork, pine nuts, eggs, breadcrumbs, parsley, lemon zest and 1 tsp salt into large oval meatballs (pelotas); blanch the cabbage leaves 1 minute and wrap each pelota in a leaf.
Add the vegetables and pelotas to the pot with remaining salt and simmer gently 40 minutes until the pelotas are cooked through.
Serve the broth first (often with a few fideos cooked in it), then the chickpeas, vegetables, meats and pelotas, as at Christmas in Alicante.

ingredients: 1 Spanish baguette (barra), cut in 2 and split
250 g beef or veal fillet, thinly sliced
steps: Fry the onion in 2 tbsp oil over medium-low heat for 12 minutes until soft and caramelised; season.
Season the beef and sear on a very hot griddle with the remaining oil for 1 minute per side until browned; warm the ham on the griddle 20 seconds.
Fill the bread with beef, ham and onion, press shut and toast briefly on the griddle; serve hot, Valencian almuerzo style.

1 tsp ground cinnamon mixed with 2 tbsp sugar
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and oil a 30 × 40 cm tin (llanda).
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 5 minutes until pale, then whisk in milk, oil and lemon zest.
Fold in the sifted flour and baking powder until smooth, pour into the tin and sprinkle with the cinnamon sugar.
Bake 30–35 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean; cool and cut into squares, served with horchata or coffee.

Bake at 180°C for 12–15 minutes until pale golden.
Glaze with icing sugar mixed with 2 tbsp water while warm, or dust with icing sugar; dunk in horchata to serve.

steps: Make a starter of the yeast, half the milk and 100 g flour and leave 30 minutes until bubbly.

Shape into 2 round loaves, rise 1 hour, brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with sugar and slash a cross on top.
Bake at 180°C for 25–30 minutes until deep brown on top (the "burnt bread"); cool on a rack and serve at Easter.

ingredients: 150 g Spanish honey (rosemary or orange blossom)
steps: Grind the almonds in a food processor for 3–5 minutes until they become an oily paste.
Heat honey and sugar in a heavy pan over low heat, stirring, for 5 minutes until dissolved; whisk the egg white to soft peaks and fold it into the hot honey.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 10–15 minutes until it thickens and turns caramel-coloured.
Stir in almond paste, cinnamon and zest and cook 5 minutes more, then press into a lined rectangular mould, cover with a weight and leave 24 hours before slicing.

ingredients: 400 g whole Marcona almonds, blanched and toasted
steps: Heat the honey over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until slightly darker; add the sugar and cook 5 minutes more until it reaches 140°C (hard crack approaching).
Whisk the egg white to stiff peaks and beat it gradually into the hot honey; continue stirring over low heat for 10 minutes until thick, pale and the mixture forms a hard ball in cold water.
Stir in the warm toasted almonds and zest quickly.
Spread between two sheets of wafer paper in a lined tin, press flat with a weight and cool 6 hours before cutting with a heavy knife.

steps: Roast the pumpkin in chunks at 200°C for 45 minutes until very soft, then scoop out the flesh, drain in a sieve for 15 minutes and mash.
Cook the mash with the sugar in a pan over low heat, stirring, for 15 minutes until thick, then cool slightly.
Beat in the ground almonds, eggs, zest and cinnamon.
Pile into a dome on a clay dish, stud with whole almonds and pine nuts in spiral patterns and bake at 180°C for 15–20 minutes until lightly golden; serve cool, a Xàtiva Easter sweet.

steps: Boil the pumpkin in a little water for 15 minutes until soft, drain well and mash; let it cool to lukewarm.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm water, then mix with pumpkin, flour, zest and salt into a soft, sticky batter; cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oil to 180°C; with wet fingers pull off walnut-sized pieces, poke a hole in the centre and drop into the oil.
Fry 2–3 minutes, turning, until golden and puffed, drain and dust with sugar; serve hot with thick chocolate during Fallas.

ingredients: 250 g dried tiger nuts (chufas, ideally DO Valencia)
1 l cold water, plus water for soaking
steps: Wash the tiger nuts well, discarding floaters, and soak in cold water in the fridge for 12–24 hours, changing the water once.
Drain, blend with 500 ml water for 2 minutes, add the remaining water and blend 1 minute more.
Strain through a fine cloth, squeezing hard, then stir in sugar (and cinnamon and peel if using) and chill 2 hours.
Remove the cinnamon and peel, serve very cold or half-frozen (granizada) with fartons; drink within 2 days.

ingredients: 500 ml freshly squeezed Valencia orange juice, chilled
750 ml cava (Spanish sparkling wine), chilled, bought from licensed producers
steps: Stir the orange juice and sugar in a large jug until the sugar dissolves.
Add the gin and vodka, then pour in the cava slowly and stir gently once.
Serve at once over a little ice in wide glasses; for adults only.

steps: Pour the condensed milk into a small heatproof glass.
Brew the espresso and pour it gently over the back of a spoon so it floats in a separate layer.
Serve showing the two layers and stir before drinking.

ingredients: 4 medium courgettes (calabacín), peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium-low heat, add the onions and cook for 10 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the courgettes and salt, cover and cook gently for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and almost melting but not browned.
Beat the eggs, pour them over the vegetables and stir over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until just set and creamy.
Serve warm as a tapa or side with bread, as in the Murcian huerta.

ingredients: 2 large eggs, hard-boiled and chopped, plus 1 beaten for glazing
60 ml fino sherry or dry white wine
¼ tsp ground cinnamon and ¼ tsp black pepper
steps: Soften the onion in the olive oil over medium heat for 6 minutes, add the beef and chorizo and fry for 10 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the sherry, cinnamon, pepper and salt and simmer for 3 minutes until dry, then cool and mix in the chopped boiled eggs.
Line a 20 cm round tin with one pastry sheet, fill with the meat and cover with a round of pastry, sealing the edges.
Cut the remaining pastry into strips and coil them on top in the traditional spiral, then brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 190 °C for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden and puffed; serve warm, as sold in Murcia's bakeries.

ingredients: 1 kg rockfish such as mullet (mújol), gurnard or grouper, cleaned, plus the heads
4 dried ñora peppers, seeded (substitute 2 tbsp sweet paprika)
steps: Fry the ñoras and 3 garlic cloves in the oil in a cast-iron pot (caldero) over medium heat for 1 minute without burning, then pound them in a mortar into a paste.
In the same oil fry the tomato for 5 minutes, add the water, the ñora paste, the fish heads and salt and boil for 20 minutes, then strain the broth.
Poach the fish pieces in the strained broth over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through, lift them out and keep warm.
Add the rice, saffron and remaining crushed garlic to 1.1 l of the hot broth and simmer for 18 minutes until tender and loose.
Serve the rice first with alioli, then the fish as a second course with more alioli and potatoes if you like.

ingredients: 800 g rabbit, jointed into small pieces
24 cooked, cleaned snails (caracoles), from a jar or tin
1 tsp sweet paprika and a pinch of saffron
2 sprigs of rosemary and 1 tsp salt
steps: Heat the oil in a paella pan over medium-high heat, season the rabbit with salt and brown it for 10 to 12 minutes, adding the pepper strips halfway.
Add the garlic and tomato and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika off the heat.
Pour in the water with the saffron and snails, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes so the rabbit cooks through.
Scatter in the rice, spread it evenly and cook on high for 8 minutes, then medium-low for 10 minutes without stirring, laying the rosemary on top for the last 5 minutes.
Remove the rosemary, rest covered for 5 minutes and serve; leave out the snails for a simpler version.

ingredients: 500 g dried broad beans (habas secas), soaked 24 to 48 hours
1 ham bone or 100 g jamón serrano trimmings
steps: Drain the soaked beans and put them in a pot with 2.5 litres of cold water, the ham bone, panceta, bay leaves and chilli.
Bring to the boil, skim, then simmer covered over low heat for 2 hours, topping up with hot water as needed.
Fry the garlic in the olive oil for 1 minute, stir in the paprika off the heat and add to the pot with the chorizo and salt.
Simmer 20 to 30 minutes more until the beans are very tender and the broth is thick and red.
Serve hot in small earthenware bowls as a winter tapa.

ingredients: 1 tsp sweet paprika and a pinch of saffron
steps: Simmer the drained chickpeas in 2 litres of water for 60 minutes until nearly tender.
Meanwhile fry the onion and garlic in the olive oil for 8 minutes, add the tomato and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika off the heat.
Add the sofrito, potatoes, green beans, pumpkin, saffron and salt to the chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the pears and mint and simmer 10 minutes more until all the vegetables are tender and the pumpkin starts to thicken the broth.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot in bowls.

ingredients: 12 rosquillas marineras (ring-shaped breadsticks), or crisp grissini rings
120 g canned tuna in oil, drained
steps: Boil the potatoes and carrot in salted water for 12 minutes, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes, then drain and cool.
Mix the vegetables with the tuna, egg, mayonnaise and salt to make the ensaladilla.
Pile a generous spoonful of ensaladilla onto each rosquilla.
Top each with an anchovy fillet and serve straight away so the breadstick stays crisp.

ingredients: 16 large raw prawns, peeled with tails left on
150 ml cold beer or sparkling water
a pinch of saffron or ¼ tsp turmeric, for colour
500 ml olive or sunflower oil, for frying
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, saffron, salt and cold beer into a thick, smooth batter.
Heat the oil to 180 °C, hold each prawn by the tail and dip the body in batter, leaving the tail bare.
Fry a few at a time for 2 minutes until golden and the prawns are cooked through.
Drain on paper and serve hot with lemon, holding them by the tail like little seahorses.

ingredients: 800 g canned whole peeled tomatoes, drained and chopped (or ripe peeled tomatoes)
160 g canned tuna in olive oil, drained
steps: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and slice.
Mix the chopped tomatoes with the onion, salt and olive oil in a shallow dish.

ingredients: 2 live spiny lobsters (llagosta), about 800 g each, or 4 lobster tails

600 g boneless lamb shoulder, cut into small cubes

ingredients: 4 thick salt cod loins (bacalao), about 200 g each, skin on
250 ml mild extra-virgin olive oil (arbequina works well)
1 dried guindilla chilli (or a pinch of chilli flakes), sliced into rings
steps: Desalt the cod in plenty of cold water in the fridge for 24–36 hours, changing the water every 8 hours, then pat it very dry; fresh cod lightly salted for 30 minutes is a substitute.
Warm the oil in a wide earthenware cazuela over low heat, add garlic and guindilla and cook gently until the garlic is pale gold, about 3 minutes; lift them out and set aside.
Let the oil cool slightly, then add the cod skin side up and poach on the lowest heat for 4 minutes per side, without letting the oil bubble, until the flakes just separate.

Remove the cod, pour the oil into a jug and let it cool for 5 minutes; return the cod to the cazuela and add the oil back in a thin stream while swirling the pan constantly in circles (or whisking the gelatinous juices with a strainer) until the sauce emulsifies into a thick, pale yellow pil-pil.
Scatter the garlic, guindilla and parsley over and serve straight from the cazuela with crusty bread.

ingredients: 4 salt cod loins (bacalao), about 180 g each, desalted
8 dried choricero peppers (or 3 tbsp choricero pepper paste)
steps: Desalt the cod in cold water in the fridge for 24–36 hours, changing the water three times; soak the choricero peppers in warm water for 1 hour, then scrape out the flesh with a spoon.
Cook the onions and garlic in half the oil over very low heat for 40 minutes until soft and sweet but not browned; add the tomato, bread and pepper flesh and cook 10 minutes more.
Add the stock, simmer 5 minutes, then blend until smooth and pass through a sieve; the sauce should be deep brick red and velvety.
Dust the cod lightly in flour and fry skin side up in the remaining oil over medium heat for 2 minutes per side.
Spoon the Vizcaína sauce into a cazuela, nestle the cod in it and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the fish flakes; serve hot with bread.

ingredients: 4 salt cod loins (bacalao), about 200 g each, desalted
2 tbsp choricero pepper paste (or 1 tsp sweet smoked paprika)

Make a pil-pil: confit garlic and guindilla in the oil over low heat until golden, remove, then poach the cod in the warm oil for 4 minutes per side; remove and emulsify the cooled oil and fish juices by swirling the pan until thick.
In another pan with 3 tbsp of the oil, slowly cook the onions and peppers over low heat for 25 minutes until very soft, then add tomato and choricero paste and cook 10 minutes into a thick pisto.
Stir the pisto into the pil-pil emulsion off the heat until combined and orange-tinted.
Return the cod to the sauce, warm through over the lowest heat for 3 minutes and serve with bread, as the Club Ranero of Bilbao made it famous.

ingredients: 200 g salt cod, desalted and flaked
steps: Desalt the cod in cold water in the fridge for 24 hours, changing the water three times, then squeeze dry and flake, removing bones.

ingredients: 12 piquillo peppers from a jar, whole
300 g salt cod, desalted and flaked

steps: Desalt the cod in cold water in the fridge for 24 hours, changing the water three times, then squeeze dry and flake finely.

Cool the filling slightly, then spoon it into the piquillo peppers, reserving 3 peppers for the sauce.

ingredients: 600 g fresh bonito del norte or albacore tuna, cut in 3 cm cubes
800 g potatoes, peeled and broken into chunks (cascadas)
2 tbsp choricero pepper paste (or 1 tsp sweet paprika)
steps: Sauté the onion, green pepper and garlic in olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the tomato and choricero paste and cook 3 minutes, then add the potatoes, snapping them so the starch thickens the broth, and stir to coat.
Pour in the stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes until the potatoes are tender.

ingredients: 2 live spider crabs (txangurro), about 1 kg each, or 400 g cooked crab meat
steps: Cook the crabs in boiling salted water for 15–18 minutes (about 15 minutes per kg), drain, cool and pick out all the meat and brown roe, reserving the cleaned top shells.
Gently cook onion, leek and carrot in olive oil over low heat for 20 minutes until soft; add tomato and cook 10 minutes more.
Add the crab meat, pour in the brandy and flame it carefully (or simply boil 2 minutes to evaporate), then stir in parsley and cook 5 minutes.
Fill the shells (or ramekins) with the mixture, sprinkle with breadcrumbs and dot with butter.
Gratinate under a hot grill for 4–5 minutes until golden and serve at once.

ingredients: 500 g hake kokotxas (hake throat cheeks), or cod kokotxas
steps: Warm the oil in a cazuela over low heat, add the garlic and guindilla and cook gently until the garlic turns pale gold, about 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat for 1 minute, then add the salted kokotxas skin side down in one layer.
Return to very low heat and swirl the cazuela continuously for 4–5 minutes; the gelatine from the kokotxas will thicken the oil into a sauce, adding a splash of stock whenever it gets too thick.
Turn the kokotxas, add the parsley and keep swirling 2 minutes more until the fish is opaque and the green sauce is creamy; serve in the cazuela.

ingredients: 100 ml dry white wine (txakoli is ideal)
150 g green peas or 8 white asparagus tips
steps: Salt the hake steaks and leave 10 minutes while you heat the oil in a cazuela over low heat and cook the garlic until fragrant but not coloured, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute, then add the wine and stock, stirring until smooth and lightly thickened.
Lay in the hake and clams, add peas, and cook over low heat for 4 minutes, shaking the cazuela so the sauce binds with the fish's gelatine.
Turn the hake, add the parsley and cook 3–4 minutes more until the fish is just opaque at the bone and the clams have opened (discard any that stay closed).
Garnish with egg and serve straight from the cazuela.

ingredients: 8 white asparagus spears from a jar, halved
steps: Season the hake with salt and dust lightly with flour; warm the oil in a cazuela over medium-low and cook the garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add the hake and seal 1 minute per side, then pour in the wine and let it bubble 1 minute before adding the stock.
Add the clams and peas and cook over low heat for 6–8 minutes, swirling the pan so the sauce thickens, until the clams open and the hake is opaque through.
Lay the asparagus and eggs on top, scatter parsley and warm 1 minute more; serve in the cazuela as they do in Zarautz.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 large hake head/neck piece (cogote), about 1 kg, split open (ask the fishmonger)
2 tbsp cider vinegar or white wine vinegar
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C, season the cogote with salt, brush with a little oil and roast skin side down on a tray for 15–20 minutes until the flesh flakes easily at the thickest part.
Meanwhile, fry the garlic and guindilla in the remaining oil over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, add the vinegar carefully (it will spit), and swirl to make a Bilbaína sizzle.
Pour the hot garlic oil over the roasted cogote, sprinkle parsley and serve, picking the sweet meat from around the bones.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg small squid (chipirones), cleaned, tentacles reserved
steps: Chop the tentacles and wings, sauté them in 2 tbsp oil for 3 minutes, then stuff them back into the squid bodies and close each with a toothpick.
Slowly cook the onions, pepper and garlic in the remaining oil over low heat for 30 minutes until jammy; add tomato and bread and cook 5 minutes.
Add the wine and the ink dissolved in the stock, simmer 5 minutes, then blend and sieve into a glossy black sauce.
Sear the stuffed squid in a hot pan for 1 minute per side, then add them to the sauce and simmer gently, covered, for 25–30 minutes until tender.
Serve with white rice or fried bread triangles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g angulas (baby eels), or the sustainable surimi substitute gulas
steps: Use individual earthenware cazuelitas; divide the oil, garlic and guindilla between them and heat over medium heat until the garlic starts to turn golden, about 2 minutes.
Add the angulas (already cooked, as sold) and a pinch of salt and stir with a wooden fork for 30–60 seconds until piping hot and sizzling.
Serve immediately, still bubbling, eaten with a wooden fork so they don't scorch the tongue; note wild angulas are very expensive and endangered, so gulas are the everyday choice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 bone-in rib steak from an older cow (txuleta de vaca vieja), about 1.2 kg and 5 cm thick
2 Gernika peppers or padrón peppers, to serve
steps: Take the steak out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking so it reaches room temperature, and dry the surface thoroughly.

Heat a charcoal grill or very heavy cast-iron pan until smoking hot; grill the steak (no salt yet) for 5–7 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms, standing it on the fat edge for 1–2 minutes to render.
Rest the steak 5 minutes, then slice off the bone into thick strips; it should be well seared outside and rare (at least 52°C) inside, as in the Basque cider houses.
Season generously with coarse salt and serve on a hot plate alongside fried peppers in olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g beef chuck or shin, cut in 4 cm cubes
3 tbsp choricero pepper paste (or 1 tbsp sweet paprika)
steps: Season the beef and brown in batches in the oil in a heavy pot over high heat, about 6 minutes per batch; set aside.
Lower the heat and cook onions, pepper, garlic and carrots for 12 minutes until soft; stir in the choricero paste.
Return the meat, add wine and let it reduce 3 minutes, then add stock and bay leaf, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer 25 minutes more until both meat and potatoes are fork-tender and the sauce is thick; serve hot, as at Basque village festivals.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g perretxikos (St George's mushrooms), or chanterelles/oyster mushrooms
steps: Brush the mushrooms clean (don't wash them) and slice the larger ones.
Warm the oil in a frying pan over medium heat, add garlic and cook 1 minute, then add the mushrooms and sauté for 4–5 minutes until their moisture evaporates and they are tender.
Lower the heat, pour in the lightly beaten, salted eggs and stir slowly with a wooden spoon for 2 minutes until just set but still creamy and loose.
Sprinkle parsley and serve immediately with bread — a spring delicacy in Álava.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 green peppers (or Espelette-style mild green peppers), sliced
1 pinch Espelette pepper or sweet paprika
steps: Cook the onions and garlic in olive oil over low heat for 10 minutes until translucent.
Add the peppers and cook 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and sweet.
Add the tomatoes, salt and Espelette pepper and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until thick and saucy.
Make four hollows, crack in the eggs (or stir them through for a scrambled version), cover and cook 4–5 minutes until the whites are set; serve with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g Gernika peppers (Gernikako piperra), or padrón peppers
steps: Wash the peppers and dry them very thoroughly so the oil doesn't spit.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat, add the peppers and fry for 5–7 minutes, turning, until blistered and soft.
Drain briefly, sprinkle with flaky salt and serve hot as a side to meat or fish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 leeks (porrua), white and pale green parts, cut in 3 cm pieces
3 potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
steps: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium-low heat and cook the garlic and leeks for 8 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Add the carrots and potatoes (snapping them into chunks) and stir 2 minutes.
Pour in the water or stock, season with salt, bring to a boil and simmer for 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and slightly thicken the broth.
Rest 5 minutes and serve hot; Basques often add desalted cod, but this version is fully vegetarian.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g salt cod, desalted and flaked
250 g stale country bread, thinly sliced
3 tbsp choricero pepper paste (or 1 tbsp sweet paprika)
steps: Desalt the cod in cold water in the fridge for 24 hours, changing the water three times, then squeeze dry, remove bones and flake it.
Fry the garlic and guindilla in olive oil in an earthenware pot over low heat until golden, about 3 minutes; add the choricero paste and stir 1 minute.
Add the bread and cod, stir to coat, then pour in the water or stock and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the bread breaks down into a thick soup.
Crack the eggs into the soup if using, cover and cook 4 minutes until the whites set; serve piping hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g Tolosa black beans (or black turtle beans)
2 morcilla de verdura (Basque blood sausage) or 2 morcillas
steps: Soak the beans overnight in cold water, drain, and put them in a pot with the water, onion, pepper and oil; bring slowly to a simmer.

Simmer very gently, partly covered, for 2–3 hours, adding a splash of cold water (asustar) three times to keep the skins intact, until the beans are creamy; then remove the onion and pepper, blend them and stir back in.
Meanwhile, simmer the chorizo, morcilla and pork belly in a separate pot of water for 30 minutes (morcilla 15 minutes so it doesn't burst) until cooked through.
Boil the cabbage in salted water for 15 minutes, drain and fry briefly in oil with garlic if you like.
Season the beans, serve them first, with the sacramentos (meats) and cabbage alongside, plus pickled guindillas.

ingredients: 8 Cantabrian anchovy fillets in olive oil
steps: Thread onto each cocktail stick: an olive, a folded guindilla, an anchovy fillet folded or rolled, a second guindilla piece and a final olive.
Arrange on a plate, drizzle with a little olive oil and serve with a cold drink, eaten in one bite, as at Donostia's pintxo bars.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g fine yellow cornmeal (masa harina works best)
400 g chistorra sausage (or thin fresh chorizo)
steps: Mix the cornmeal and salt, add the warm water gradually and knead until you have a smooth, pliable dough; rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 4 balls and pat or press each between sheets of baking paper into thin 18 cm rounds.
Cook each talo on a dry, hot griddle or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side until dry and lightly spotted.
Fry the chistorra in the oil over medium heat for 5–6 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Wrap the hot chistorra in the talo and eat at once, as at the Santo Tomás fair in Donostia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp rum syrup (2 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp water, 1 tbsp rum)
steps: Whisk 4 eggs with 100 g sugar until thick and pale, about 8 minutes, fold in the flour and bake in a lined tray at 180°C for 12 minutes; cool and cut rounds to fit your glasses.
Heat the milk with vanilla; whisk the 4 yolks with 70 g sugar and the cornflour, pour on the hot milk, return to the pan and stir over medium heat until thick, about 3 minutes; cover and chill.
Whip the cream with 20 g sugar to soft peaks and pipe a layer into the bottom of each glass, then add a round of sponge moistened with rum syrup.
Top with the custard, sprinkle the remaining 30 g sugar and caramelise with a blowtorch or under a very hot grill; serve cold, a Vitoria classic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 large egg yolks, plus 1 egg for glazing
steps: Make a crème pâtissière: heat the milk with vanilla, whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour, pour on the hot milk, then return to the pan and stir over medium heat for 3 minutes until thick; cover and cool completely.
Line a 24 cm tin with one pastry sheet, spread the cold custard over it and cover with the second sheet, sealing the edges.
Brush with beaten egg, press the flaked almonds all over and prick a few steam holes.
Bake at 200°C for 30–35 minutes until puffed and deep golden; cool, dust with icing sugar and serve in wedges, as created in Donostia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 large eggs, plus 4 yolks and 1 egg for glazing
steps: Beat the butter with 150 g sugar until light, add 2 eggs, then mix in the flour, almonds and salt to a soft dough; wrap and chill 1 hour.
Make the cream: heat milk with vanilla, whisk 4 yolks with 50 g sugar and cornflour, pour on the hot milk and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes until thick; stir in rum and cool.
Roll two-thirds of the dough to line a buttered 24 cm tin, fill with the cold cream and cover with the remaining dough rolled into a lid, sealing the edges well.
Brush with beaten egg and score a crosshatch with a fork; bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until golden brown.
Cool completely in the tin before slicing; black cherry jam can replace the cream for the traditional variant.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a 24 cm springform tin with two crumpled sheets of baking paper that rise well above the rim.
Beat the cream cheese with the sugar and salt until smooth, then add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each.
Pour in the cream and sift in the flour, mixing just until smooth, then strain the batter into the tin.
Bake for 45–50 minutes until the top is deep brown, almost black, and the centre still wobbles strongly when shaken.
Cool at room temperature for 2 hours (it will sink), then serve at room temperature or chilled, in the style of La Viña in Donostia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring the milk to a gentle simmer with the cinnamon and lemon peel in a heavy pan.
Add the ground walnuts and salt and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't catch, until it thickens like a loose porridge.
Stir in the sugar and cook 10 minutes more until creamy, then remove the cinnamon and peel.
Serve warm or chilled in small bowls; it is the traditional Christmas Eve dessert in Gipuzkoa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Make a thick crème pâtissière: heat the milk with vanilla, whisk yolks, sugar and cornflour, pour on the hot milk, return to the pan and stir over medium heat for 3 minutes until thick; cover and chill.
Cut the pastry into 2 cm strips and wrap them in overlapping spirals around greased cream-horn moulds (canutillo tubes).
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C for 15–18 minutes until golden and crisp; cool, then slide off the moulds.
Pipe the cold custard into each tube and dust with icing sugar; serve the same day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 large egg yolks, plus 4 egg whites
steps: Line 8 small tartlet moulds with the pastry, prick and blind-bake at 180°C for 15 minutes until golden; cool.
Make a custard by heating the milk with vanilla, whisking in yolks, 60 g sugar and cornflour and stirring over medium heat until thick; fill the tartlets and cool.
Make an Italian meringue: boil 240 g sugar with 80 ml water to 118°C, then pour in a thin stream onto the egg whites whipped with lemon juice, beating until stiff, glossy and cool.
Pipe a tall cone of meringue on each tartlet, then dip the tip of each cone into the melted chocolate (or brush with egg-yolk glaze for the classic yellow tip).
Chill 15 minutes to set before serving — a Bilbao pastry-shop favourite.
