ingredients: 70 g sugar, plus 100 g icing sugar for the filling
60 g soft butter for the dough, plus 150 g soft butter for the filling
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add eggs and milk and knead 10 minutes, then work in 60 g butter until silky; cover and leave to rise for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces, shape into oval buns, set on a tray and prove 1 hour until puffy.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 190°C for 12–15 minutes until golden; cool completely.
Beat 150 g butter with the icing sugar for 5 minutes until very light; split each bun lengthwise and spread thickly with the butter cream — a Bilbao breakfast staple.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 ml young red wine, from a licensed producer
steps: Fill two tall glasses with ice.
Pour in equal parts red wine and cola and stir gently once so it doesn't go flat.
Garnish with lemon and serve immediately, as at Basque fiestas; a non-alcoholic version uses alcohol-free red wine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 octopus (about 2 kg), previously frozen and thawed, or tenderised
2 tsp sweet pimentón (pimentón de la Vera)
steps: Bring a large pot of unsalted water with the onion and bay leaf to a rolling boil; holding the octopus by the head, dip it in and lift it out 3 times ("asustar") so the tentacles curl.
Drop it in and simmer 40–50 minutes until a skewer slides easily into the thickest tentacle; leave it in the water off the heat for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in some of the octopus water for 20–25 minutes until tender, then peel and slice thickly.
Cut the tentacles into 1 cm coins with scissors and arrange over the potatoes on a wooden plate.
Sprinkle with sea salt and both pimentóns and drizzle with olive oil; serve warm with bread, as at Galician fairs (pulpo á feira).

ingredients: 80 ml oil from the filling sofrito
2 tins (240 g drained) tuna in oil, or 400 g cooked shredded pork loin
steps: Fry onions, peppers and garlic in the olive oil over low heat for 30 minutes until very soft and sweet; stir in the pimentón, then drain, reserving the coloured oil.
Dissolve the yeast in the water and mix with flour, 1 tsp salt and 80 ml of the reserved oil; knead 8 minutes and rest 1 hour.

Mix the tuna (or pork) into the sofrito; roll half the dough thinly to line a 30 cm oiled tray, spread the filling, lay the egg slices on top and cover with the remaining rolled dough, crimping the edges.
Cut a small steam hole, brush with beaten egg and bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until golden; cool slightly and serve warm or cold in squares.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg lacón (salt-cured pork shoulder), desalted 24–48 hours in cold water with changes
1.5 kg grelos (turnip tops), tough stems removed (or rapini/broccoli rabe)
steps: Put the desalted lacón in a large pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer gently for 2 hours until tender.
Add the chorizos and potatoes and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the grelos and cook 10–15 minutes until tender but still green; check for salt (the lacón usually provides enough).
Drain, slice the lacón and chorizo and serve on a platter with the grelos and potatoes, dusted with pimentón and drizzled with olive oil; this is the classic Carnival (Entroido) dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g dried white beans (fabas), soaked overnight
300 g salted pork rib (costilla salada), desalted
150 g unto (cured pork fat) or salt pork
4 potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks (cachelos)
500 g grelos or berzas (collard greens / cabbage), shredded
steps: Simmer the beans, rib, unto and ham bone in the water for 1 hour 30 minutes, skimming.
Add the potatoes, broken rather than cut so they release starch, and cook 20 minutes.
Add the greens and cook 20 minutes more until tender; adjust salt and remove the bone.
Rest the soup 10 minutes (it is better the next day) and serve hot in clay bowls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg lacón or salted pork shoulder, desalted 24 hours
steps: Put beef, lacón, tocino and chicken in the cold water, bring to a boil, skim and simmer 1 hour.
Add the chickpeas in a net bag and simmer 1 hour 30 minutes more until the meats and chickpeas are tender.
Cook the chorizos, potatoes and grelos separately in some of the broth for 25 minutes so the main broth stays clear.
Serve the broth first as soup (often with fine noodles), then a platter of meats, chickpeas, potatoes and greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg firm white fish (hake, monkfish, ray or conger), cut in thick steaks
800 g potatoes, peeled and sliced 1 cm thick
steps: Boil the potatoes, onion and bay leaves in the salted water for 15 minutes until almost tender.
Lay the fish on top and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the flesh flakes and is opaque throughout.
Meanwhile fry the garlic in the oil over low heat 2 minutes until golden; off the heat stir in the pimentón and vinegar (this is the ajada).
Drain the fish and potatoes, arrange in a dish and pour the hot ajada over; serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rinse and dry the peppers thoroughly.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat until shimmering and fry the peppers 4–5 minutes, turning, until blistered and soft.
Drain briefly, sprinkle generously with salt and serve hot — "uns pican e outros non" (some are hot, some are not).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Put the potatoes in cold water with the salt and bay leaf and bring to a boil.
Simmer 20–25 minutes until a knife slides in easily; drain and let them steam dry 2 minutes.
Peel if liked, cut into thick chunks and serve drizzled with olive oil and a dusting of pimentón, alongside octopus, fish or lacón.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 24 zamburiñas (small variegated scallops) on the half shell (or queen scallops)
steps: Mix garlic, parsley and olive oil into a loose sauce.
Heat a griddle over high heat and place the scallops in their shells on it.
Spoon a little sauce over each and cook 3–4 minutes until the flesh turns opaque and the sauce sizzles.
Season with salt and a squeeze of lemon and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 large king scallops (vieiras) in their shells, cleaned
steps: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil over low heat for 12 minutes until soft and golden, then add the ham for 2 minutes.
Add pimentón and wine and simmer 3 minutes until reduced.
Place each scallop with its coral in a cleaned deep shell, spoon the sauce over and sprinkle with breadcrumbs and parsley.
Bake at 200°C for 8–10 minutes until the scallops are just opaque and the crumbs are golden; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Stand the razor clams upright in cold salted water for 1 hour to purge sand; rinse.
Mix garlic, parsley and olive oil.
Lay the clams on a very hot griddle in a single layer and cook 2–3 minutes until they open, spooning over the garlic oil.
Season with salt and lemon and serve at once; discard any that don't open.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg live clams (almejas, ideally from Carril)
steps: Soak the clams in cold salted water for 2 hours to purge sand, changing the water once.
Fry onion and garlic in the oil over low heat for 8 minutes until soft, stir in the flour and pimentón for 1 minute.
Add the wine and stock, simmer 2 minutes, then add the clams, cover and cook on high heat 3–4 minutes until they open.
Sprinkle with parsley, discard any unopened clams and serve with bread for the sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fresh goose barnacles (percebes, from the Costa da Morte)
steps: Bring the water with salt and bay leaf to a fierce rolling boil.
Add the percebes, wait for the water to return to a boil and cook 1 minute more.
Drain and serve warm on a plate covered with a cloth; twist off the nail and pull out the pink flesh to eat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g xoubas (small sardines), gutted and heads removed
steps: Rinse and dry the sardines thoroughly and season with salt.
Toss in flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil to 180°C and fry in batches for 2–3 minutes until crisp and golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper and serve hot with lemon and a slice of corn bread (broa).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Chill the crab in the freezer for 20 minutes to make it dormant, then put it into cold salted water with the bay leaf and bring to a boil.
Cook 15–18 minutes from boiling until the shell is bright red; drain and cool upside down.
Open the body, scoop out the meat and the brown coral (corales) into a bowl, crack the legs and extract the meat.
Mix the meat and coral with onion, parsley, egg and oil, pile back into the cleaned shell and serve with the legs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thick hake steaks (rodajas), about 200 g each
800 g potatoes, peeled and sliced 1 cm thick
steps: Boil the potatoes, onion and bay leaf in salted water for 15 minutes.
Add the hake and simmer gently 6–8 minutes until opaque and just flaking.
Fry the garlic in the oil over low heat until golden, remove from heat and stir in pimentón and vinegar (ajada).
Plate the hake and potatoes, pour over the hot ajada and serve with a spoon of the cooking broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 lamprey (about 1.2 kg), bled with blood reserved, cleaned and cut into chunks (or eel)
steps: Scald the lamprey quickly in boiling water to scrape off the slime, remove the cartilage cord (bile string), then cut into 5 cm pieces and mix with the reserved blood and the wine; marinate 30 minutes.
Fry onions, leek and garlic in the oil in a clay pot over low heat for 20 minutes until soft.
Add the lamprey with its wine and blood, season and simmer gently for 45–60 minutes until tender and the sauce is thick and dark.
Stir in parsley and serve over fried bread with white rice, as in Arbo during the spring lamprey festival.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef (tenreira gallega) shank or brisket, in large pieces
steps: Put the beef, onion, bay leaf and salt in a large pot (caldeiro) of cold water, bring to a boil, skim and simmer 1 hour 30 minutes until tender.
Add the potatoes and cook 25 minutes more.
Drain, cut the beef into bite-sized pieces and the potatoes into chunks and arrange on a wooden plate.
Sprinkle with salt and pimentóns and drizzle with olive oil, like pulpo á feira.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g pork loin, cut into 2 cm cubes
600 g potatoes, cut into chips and fried
steps: Marinate the pork with garlic, pimentón, oregano, salt and wine for 2 hours in the fridge.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat and fry the drained pork for 8–10 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the marinade and simmer 2 minutes to make a little sauce.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with chips (raxo con patacas).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 700 g pork shoulder, cut into small pieces
4 fried eggs and fried potatoes to serve
steps: Mix the pork with garlic, both pimentóns, oregano, wine and salt (this is the raw chorizo filling) and marinate in the fridge for 24 hours, stirring once.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the zorza for 10–12 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with fried eggs and potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Fry the potatoes slowly in the oil over medium-low heat for 20 minutes until soft but not coloured; drain well, reserving the oil, and season.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and fold in the hot potatoes; rest 5 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a 22 cm pan over high heat, pour in the mixture and cook 1 minute, then flip with a plate and cook 30 seconds more.
Serve immediately with the centre runny (pouco callada); use very fresh eggs as the centre stays soft.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a 24 cm round tin.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then fold in almonds, zest and cinnamon.
Pour into the tin and bake 35–40 minutes until golden and set.
Cool, place a cross of Santiago stencil on top and dust with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 ml water (or meat broth for savoury)
30 g butter or a piece of pork fat (unto) for greasing
4 tbsp sugar or honey to serve
steps: Whisk flour, eggs, milk, water and salt to a very thin smooth batter and rest 30 minutes.
Heat a crêpe pan (filloeira) over medium-high heat and grease lightly with butter.
Pour in a small ladle, swirl to a paper-thin layer and cook 1 minute until lacy, then flip 20 seconds.
Stack and serve sprinkled with sugar or drizzled with honey, folded or filled with custard, especially at Entroido.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 20 × 30 cm tin.
Beat the butter and sugar until creamy, then add the eggs one by one, then the cream.
Fold in sifted flour and baking powder, pour into the tin and sprinkle the top with sugar.
Bake 45–50 minutes until golden with a cracked sugary crust; cool and cut into squares, as in Laza and Trives.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp anís liqueur (or orange blossom water)
steps: Mix flour, eggs, butter, milk, anís, zest and salt into a smooth firm dough and rest 1 hour.
Roll very thinly (1–2 mm) and cut into ear-shaped pieces about 10 cm long.
Fry in oil at 180°C for 30–40 seconds per side until golden and blistered.
Drain and dust with icing sugar while warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 l orujo (Galician grape pomace spirit, augardente), bought from licensed producers
steps: Pour the orujo into a clay pot (pote de barro) on a fireproof surface away from anything flammable, and add most of the sugar, lemon peel and coffee beans.
Put a ladle of orujo with a spoon of sugar on top, light it carefully and lower it into the pot to set the whole surface aflame.
Stir and lift ladles of flaming liquor for about 5–10 minutes while reciting the conxuro, until the flames turn blue and weaken.
Cover the pot to extinguish the flames, let it cool a moment and serve warm in small clay cups; for adults only.

100 g freshly roasted whole coffee beans

Heat the sugar and water over medium heat for 5 minutes until a clear syrup forms; cool and add to the jar.
Seal and macerate in a dark place for 2 weeks, shaking every few days.

ingredients: 500 g fabes de la granja (large Asturian white beans), or butter beans
200 g lacón or smoked ham hock
steps: Soak the beans overnight in cold water, and soak the lacón and tocino separately to remove excess salt.
Put the beans in a wide pot, cover with the cold water by two fingers, add the lacón, tocino, chorizo and morcilla (the compango) and bring slowly to a boil, skimming the foam.

Lower the heat to a bare simmer, add saffron and paprika and cook partly covered for 2.5–3 hours; never stir with a spoon — shake the pot instead — and add a splash of cold water (asustar) whenever the beans come above the liquid.
When the beans are buttery-soft and the broth creamy, check salt, rest 15 minutes off the heat, then slice the meats and serve on top of the beans with Asturian cider.

ingredients: 1/2 head berza (Asturian collard/kale) or savoy cabbage, shredded
steps: Simmer the soaked beans in the water with the tocino, pork, chorizo and morcilla for 1.5 hours, skimming foam and shaking the pot rather than stirring.
Meanwhile, blanch the shredded berza in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and add it to the pot.
Add the potatoes and paprika and simmer 30–40 minutes more until the potatoes and beans are tender and the broth is thick.
Check salt, rest 10 minutes and serve in deep bowls with the sliced meats.

ingredients: 500 g fabes (large white beans), soaked overnight
500 g clams, purged in salted water for 1 hour
steps: Cover the soaked beans with cold water by two fingers, add the onion, pepper and 2 tbsp oil and simmer very gently for 2–2.5 hours, adding cold water a few times, until creamy.
Remove onion and pepper, blend them with a ladle of beans and stir back in with the saffron.
Fry the garlic in the remaining oil in a pan until golden, add the clams and wine, cover and cook 3–4 minutes until they open (discard closed ones).
Tip the clams with their juices and parsley into the beans, shake the pot and simmer 5 minutes; rest 10 minutes and serve.

ingredients: 400 g verdinas (small green Asturian beans), or flageolet beans
200 g squid, cleaned and cut in rings
steps: Soak the verdinas overnight, then cover with the fish stock and simmer gently for 60–75 minutes until tender, adding cold water as needed.
Sauté onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes until soft, add the squid and cook 5 minutes.
Stir the sofrito and saffron into the beans and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the clams and prawns, cover and cook 4–5 minutes until the clams open and the prawns are pink; rest 5 minutes and serve.

ingredients: 2 large thin veal fillets (about 200 g each), pounded to 5 mm
4 slices melting cheese (Asturian Afuega'l Pitu or Gouda-style)

Dredge the cachopo in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing well, and chill 10 minutes.

ingredients: 4 cooking chorizos asturianos (semi-cured), cut in thick slices or left whole

Pour in the cider, add the bay leaf and bring to a boil.

steps: Season the hake with salt and dust lightly with flour.

ingredients: 800 g monkfish (pixín) tail, cut in medallions

ingredients: 1 scorpion fish (cabracho), about 1 kg, cleaned — or 600 g gurnard or cod fillets
1 leek, 1 carrot and 1 bay leaf for poaching
steps: Poach the fish with leek, carrot and bay in simmering salted water for 15 minutes until cooked through; cool, then remove all skin and bones and flake the flesh.

steps: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat and add the crumbled Cabrales.

ingredients: 1 bottle (700 ml) Asturian sidra natural from a licensed producer (DOP Sidra de Asturias)
200 g Asturian cheese and chorizo, to accompany
steps: Sidra natural is Asturias's still, dry, tart cider made from local apples; buy it from licensed cider makers (llagares) rather than making it at home.

ingredients: 500 g chickpeas (garbanzos de Potes), soaked overnight

steps: Bring the water with the beef and pork belly to a boil, skim, then add the soaked chickpeas in a net and simmer gently for 2.5 hours until tender.

ingredients: 600 g bonito del norte (albacore tuna), cubed
800 g potatoes, peeled and broken into chunks
steps: Cook the onion, pepper and garlic in olive oil over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until soft.

Lay a slice of bread in each bowl and ladle the stew over it; this is the fishermen's dish of San Vicente de la Barquera.

ingredients: 600 g squid (calamares or chipirones), cleaned and cut into strips

steps: Dry the squid strips thoroughly and season with salt.

ingredients: 500 g fresh anchovies (bocartes), cleaned and opened butterfly-style, spines removed

ingredients: 1.5 kg ternasco de Aragón (young milk-fed lamb) shoulder or leg, cut in large pieces (substitute spring lamb)
800 g potatoes, peeled and sliced 1 cm thick
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and lay the potato slices in an earthenware roasting dish (cazuela de barro), season with a pinch of salt and drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil.

Pour the wine and water around the meat, drizzle with the remaining oil and roast for 45 minutes, basting twice.
Turn the pieces skin-side up, raise the oven to 210°C and roast 40–45 minutes more until the skin is golden and crackling and the meat pulls easily from the bone (at least 70°C inside).

ingredients: 400 g day-old rustic country bread, cut in small dice

4 eggs, to serve fried on top
steps: The night before, sprinkle the bread dice with the salted water, toss, wrap in a damp cloth and leave to soften overnight.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat, fry the garlic until golden, then fry the panceta and chorizo for 6–8 minutes until crisp; lift out and keep warm.

Add the bread to the flavoured fat, sprinkle with pimentón and cook over medium-low heat, turning and chopping constantly with a spatula, for 15–20 minutes until the crumbs are loose, golden and slightly crisp.

steps: Season the chicken with salt and brown it in the olive oil in a wide cazuela over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes until golden on all sides; set aside.

Add the tomato, choricero pulp and bay leaf and cook 10 minutes until jammy.

ingredients: 2 dried choricero peppers, soaked and flesh scraped (substitute 1 tsp sweet pimentón)
steps: Soak the cod in cold water in the fridge for 24–36 hours, changing the water 3–4 times, then drain, remove skin and bones and flake it.

Dip each leaf in the batter, let the excess drip off and fry 1–2 minutes per side until puffed and golden.

1 tbsp cocoa butter or neutral oil

steps: Knead the flour, yeast, milk, 2 eggs, sugar and a pinch of salt for 8 minutes, then work in the butter until the dough is smooth and elastic; rise covered for 1.5 hours until doubled.

ingredients: 100 g sugar (for cream) plus 3 tbsp water

ingredients: 12 roasted piquillo peppers from a jar (Pimiento del Piquillo de Lodosa)

ingredients: 6 artichokes, trimmed to hearts and quartered
250 g green beans, cut in pieces
200 g white asparagus spears, cut in pieces

steps: Cook each vegetable separately in boiling salted water until just tender (beans 6 min, peas 4, artichokes 12, asparagus 8, chard 8), draining and reserving 300 ml cooking liquid.

steps: Season the inside of each trout with salt and tuck two slices of jamón into the cavity.

ingredients: 1 kg fresh thick white asparagus (Espárrago de Navarra), or 2 jars good preserved white asparagus

steps: Trim the artichokes down to the tender hearts, halve them and rub with lemon, dropping them into lemon water to stop browning.

ingredients: 4 cogollos de Tudela (small lettuce hearts), quartered lengthwise (substitute Little Gem)

steps: Warm the milk in a saucepan over low heat to 37–40°C (blood heat); do not let it get hotter.
Remove from heat, stir in the rennet for a few seconds and immediately pour into four small clay pots (cuajaderas).

ingredients: 1 litre anise liqueur (anís dulce or seco), bought from licensed producers

steps: Pacharán is Navarre's sloe-flavoured anise liqueur; commercial bottles (Pacharán Navarro) are sold by licensed producers and can simply be bought ready to drink.
For the traditional home infusion, put the sloes, cinnamon and coffee beans into a clean glass jar or bottle and cover with the bought anise liqueur.

ingredients: 250 g fresh chorizo riojano, sliced thick
1 dried choricero pepper, soaked and flesh scraped (substitute 1 tsp sweet pimentón)
steps: Soften the onion, green pepper and garlic in the oil in a pot over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the chorizo and fry 3 minutes until its red fat releases, then stir in the choricero pulp.
Break the potatoes into chunks by cutting partway and snapping (cascar) so they release starch, add them and stir to coat.
Pour in the water with the bay leaf and salt, bring to the boil and simmer 25–30 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the broth slightly thickened.

ingredients: 800 g fresh pochas (shelled fresh white haricot beans), or 300 g dried white beans soaked overnight
steps: Cover the beans with cold water in a pot with half the onion, the green pepper, garlic and 2 tbsp oil, bring to a gentle simmer and cook 35–40 minutes (longer for soaked dried beans) until creamy, adding cold water if they dry.
Meanwhile fry the rest of the onion in 2 tbsp oil until soft, add the tomato and chorizo and cook 10 minutes, then stir in the pimentón off the heat.
Add this sofrito to the beans, season with salt and simmer 10 minutes more without boiling hard.
Serve hot with pickled guindillas on the side.

ingredients: 400 g dried caparrones (small red beans from Anguiano), or dried red kidney beans
steps: Soak the beans in cold water overnight, then drain.
Put them in a pot with the chorizo, panceta, onion, pepper, garlic and oil, cover with cold water and bring slowly to a boil, skimming the foam (boil hard 10 minutes if using kidney beans).
Simmer very gently for 2–2.5 hours, "scaring" the beans with a splash of cold water whenever the boil rises, until creamy and tender.
Remove the onion and pepper, blend them with a ladle of broth and the pimentón and stir back to thicken.
Slice the meats, season with salt and serve with pickled guindillas.

ingredients: 1.2 kg baby lamb rib chops (chuletillas de lechal), about 24
1 large bundle dry vine cuttings (sarmientos), or hardwood charcoal
steps: Light the vine cuttings in a grill and let them burn down to glowing embers with no flames, about 15 minutes.
Brush the chops lightly with oil and season with coarse salt.
Grill on a rack over the embers for 2–3 minutes per side until well browned and cooked through with no pink juices.
Serve immediately on a platter, eaten with the fingers, with lemon wedges and a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thick pieces salt cod loin (lomo de bacalao), about 200 g each
2 dried choricero peppers, soaked and flesh scraped (substitute 1 tsp sweet pimentón)
steps: Desalt the cod in cold water in the fridge for 24–36 hours, changing the water 3–4 times, then pat dry.
Make the sauce: soften the onion and garlic in 4 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, add tomato, choricero pulp and sugar and simmer 20 minutes until thick, then blend smooth.
Flour the cod and fry in the remaining oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until lightly golden.
Lay the cod in a cazuela, cover with the sauce and the piquillo strips and simmer gently 8–10 minutes until the fish flakes; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 24 medium white button mushrooms (champiñones), stems removed
4 cooked prawns, peeled and cut in pieces
steps: Mix the garlic and parsley with 3 tbsp of oil to make a sauce (majado).
Heat a griddle (plancha) over high heat with 1 tbsp oil and lay the mushroom caps hollow-side down for 3–4 minutes until golden.
Turn them over, sprinkle with salt and fill each with a little garlic oil and a piece of prawn, and cook 3–4 minutes until juices bubble inside the cap.
Stack three mushrooms on a toothpick, stand them on a slice of bread to catch the juices, and serve at once as they do on Calle del Laurel in Logroño.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour, olive oil, wine and salt to a smooth, elastic dough and rest 20 minutes.
For the filling, combine the ground almonds, sugar, lemon zest and enough water to make a firm paste (alternatively, mazapán).
Roll the dough very thin, cut into rectangles about 10 x 5 cm, place a sausage of almond paste on each and fold over, sealing the edges with a fork.
Fry in oil at 170°C for 2–3 minutes per side until golden, drain on paper and dust with icing sugar once cool.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 suckling pig (cochinillo), about 4–5 kg, split open butterfly-style by the butcher
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C, rub the inside of the pig with salt and lay it skin-side down in a large earthenware dish on two wooden spoons or a rack so it does not touch the bottom.
Add the water, garlic and bay leaves to the dish and roast for 1 hour 30 minutes.

Turn the pig skin-side up, prick the skin all over with a fork, rub with lard and salt, and roast another 50–60 minutes at 200°C, basting with its juices, until the skin is glass-crisp and the meat reaches at least 70°C.
Rest 10 minutes and, in the Segovian style, cut into portions with the edge of a plate, serving with the pan juices and a lettuce salad.

ingredients: 1.5 kg milk-fed lamb (lechazo de Castilla y León) quarter, leg or shoulder (substitute spring lamb)
steps: Heat the oven (ideally a wood oven) to 170°C and place the lamb skin-side down in a clay cazuela with the water, salt and garlic.
Roast for 1 hour, basting with the liquid every 20 minutes.
Turn the lamb skin-side up, rub with lard and roast another 50–60 minutes at 200°C until the skin is golden and crisp and the meat comes away from the bone.
Serve in the clay dish with its juices, crusty Castilian bread and a lettuce, tomato and onion salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 Morcilla de Burgos (rice blood sausage), about 400 g, bought from a butcher
2 roasted red peppers or piquillos, in strips
steps: Cut the morcilla into 1.5 cm slices and remove the casing if you prefer them neater.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the slices for 2–3 minutes per side until crisp outside and piping hot through.
Warm the pepper strips in the same pan for 1 minute.
Serve the morcilla on bread slices topped with pepper, as a tapa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g day-old rustic bread, thinly sliced
1 tbsp sweet pimentón de la Vera
steps: In a clay cazuela heat the oil over medium-low heat and fry the garlic until pale gold, then add the jamón for 1 minute.
Add the bread slices and stir until they absorb the oil and toast lightly, about 3 minutes.
Off the heat stir in the pimentón, then immediately pour in the hot stock, season and simmer 10 minutes.
Crack the eggs into the soup, cover and poach 3–4 minutes until the whites are set, or bake in individual bowls at 200°C until set; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g pork loin, sliced and marinated in pimentón and garlic
steps: Knead the flour, yeast, 2 eggs, wine, olive oil, pimentón and a pinch of salt into a smooth dough and rest 1 hour.
Fry the marinated pork loin in a little oil over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side until cooked through; cool.
Roll half the dough to a 30 cm rectangle on a lined tray, layer the pork, chorizo, jamón and hard-boiled egg, then cover with the rest of the dough, sealing the edges.
Decorate with a lattice of dough strips, brush with beaten egg and rest 20 minutes.
Bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until deep golden; eat warm or cold, as at Salamanca's Lunes de Aguas.

ingredients: 1 botillo del Bierzo (smoked, paprika-cured stuffed pork rib sausage), about 1 kg, bought from a producer
1 small white cabbage, cut in wedges
steps: Rinse the botillo, wrap it in a cloth or cheesecloth so it holds shape, and place in a large pot of cold water with the bay leaf.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 2.5–3 hours, never at a rolling boil, until very tender.
In the last 30 minutes, add the potatoes and cabbage to the pot and cook until tender.
Lift out the botillo, open it at the table, and serve the meat with the potatoes and cabbage drizzled with olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g judiones de La Granja (giant white beans), or Greek gigantes beans
steps: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water for 12 hours, then drain.
Place them in a pot with the chorizo, panceta, pig's ear, onion, garlic and bay leaf, cover with cold water and bring slowly to a simmer.
Simmer very gently for 2–2.5 hours, adding a splash of cold water whenever it boils up, until the beans are creamy and unbroken; add the morcilla for the last 20 minutes.
Fry the pimentón briefly in the oil off the heat, stir it into the pot, season with salt and serve with the meats sliced on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork belly and cured pork shoulder (lacón), in pieces
1 relleno (dough of 2 eggs, 100 g breadcrumbs, garlic, parsley), fried
steps: Put the beef, pork, chicken and pig's ear in a large pot of water, bring to the boil and skim, then add the soaked chickpeas in a net.
Simmer gently for 2.5 hours, adding the chorizos, cabbage and potatoes for the last 40 minutes.
Shape the relleno mixture into patties, fry in oil until golden and add to the pot for 10 minutes.
Strain off the broth and cook the fideos in it for 4 minutes.
Serve in the Maragato order, reversed: first all the meats, then the chickpeas and vegetables, and finally the noodle soup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g dried red beans (alubia roja de Ibeas), soaked 12 hours
steps: Put the soaked beans with the onion, pepper and olive oil in a large pot, cover with cold water and bring to the boil for 10 minutes, skimming.
Add the ribs, ear, trotter, panceta and chorizo, lower to a bare simmer and cook 2.5 hours, adding cold water little by little to keep beans covered.
Add the morcilla for the last 20 minutes so it heats without bursting.
Remove onion and pepper, blend them with a ladle of beans and the pimentón and stir back in to thicken.
Season with salt and serve the beans first, then the meats, with pickled guindillas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
200 g panceta, cut into small strips (torreznos)
1 tbsp sweet pimentón de la Vera
steps: Boil the potatoes with the bay leaf and salt for 20–25 minutes until very tender, reserving a cup of cooking water.
Meanwhile fry the panceta strips in a pan over medium heat for 10 minutes until crisp; remove and keep.
Fry the garlic in the remaining fat and olive oil until golden, then remove from heat and stir in both pimentóns.
Mash the drained potatoes with the red oil and enough cooking water to make a smooth purée, and serve topped with the crisp torreznos.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g pig's ear and trotter, pre-cooked and diced (optional)
steps: In a clay cazuela brown the ribs and panceta in the oil over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic and turnip and cook 8 minutes until soft, then add the ear and trotter if using.
Stir in the rice and pimentón for 1 minute, then pour in the hot stock and season.
Simmer on the hob for 10 minutes, then bake at 200°C for 12–15 minutes until the rice is tender and the top is lightly crusted; rest 5 minutes and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 hard-boiled eggs, yolks and whites separated
150 ml fino sherry or dry white wine
steps: Season and flour the chicken and brown it in the oil in a cazuela over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes; set aside.
In the same oil fry the garlic and almonds until golden and remove; then soften the onion for 10 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the wine and stock, cover and simmer 30–35 minutes until cooked through.
Pound the almonds, garlic, saffron and egg yolks into a paste (majado) with a little broth and stir into the sauce, simmering 5 minutes to thicken.
Serve topped with chopped egg white and white rice or fried potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a tray with 12 square paper cases (cajitas).
Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and cinnamon until just combined.
Fill the paper cases two-thirds full, sprinkle with sugar and bake 18–20 minutes until risen with a golden crackled top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the sugar, water, lemon peel and cinnamon over medium heat to a thread syrup (about 107°C), then discard the peel and cinnamon and cool slightly.
Whisk the yolks, then add the syrup in a thin stream, whisking.
Cook over very low heat, stirring constantly, for 8–10 minutes until it thickens to a paste that leaves the sides of the pan and the eggs are fully cooked.
Cool, then roll into small balls with icing-sugared hands, coat in icing sugar and set each in a paper case.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 thin sponge sheet (bizcocho), about 30 x 20 cm
100 ml sugar syrup with 1 tbsp anise liqueur
steps: Make a pastry cream: heat the milk, whisk 2 eggs plus 2 yolks with sugar and cornflour, pour over the hot milk and cook, stirring, until thick and bubbling for 1 minute; cool.
Cut the sponge into three strips, soak each with the anise syrup, and layer them with pastry cream between.
Cover the top and sides with the thin marzipan sheet.
Dust thickly with icing sugar and mark the classic diamond lattice by pressing a red-hot skewer into the sugar to caramelise it; chill 1 hour before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat and cook the onions and garlic for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the peppers and cook 10 minutes, then the courgettes for 8 minutes more.
Stir in the tomatoes, sugar and salt and simmer gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until the vegetables are melting and the liquid has reduced.
Serve hot or warm with bread; a fried egg on top is customary for non-vegetarians but optional.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g harina de almortas (grass-pea flour), substitute chickpea flour
steps: In a wide frying pan fry the garlic, panceta, chorizo and liver in the oil over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until well cooked; set the meats aside.
Off the heat, add the flour to the oil and stir for 1–2 minutes over low heat to toast, then add the pimentón and cumin.
Pour in the water gradually, stirring constantly, and cook 10–12 minutes until thick and creamy, seasoning with salt.
Return the meats on top and eat straight from the pan with spoons or bread, as is tradition.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g day-old candeal bread, cut in small dice
steps: The night before, sprinkle the bread with salted water and wrap in a damp cloth.
Fry the garlic, peppers, panceta and chorizo in the oil in a wide pan over medium heat for 10 minutes until well cooked; remove and keep warm.
Add the bread and pimentón to the fat and cook over medium-low heat, constantly turning and cutting with a spatula, for 20 minutes until loose and golden.
Mix the meats back in and serve with grapes or melon on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Desalt the cod in cold water in the fridge for 24–36 hours, changing water several times.
Boil the potatoes in unsalted water for 20 minutes, add the cod for the last 8 minutes until it flakes, then drain, reserving some water.
In a mortar pound the garlic, add the cod and potatoes and mash, adding olive oil a little at a time and some cooking water, until it becomes a thick, smooth purée.
Serve warm decorated with hard-boiled egg and walnuts, with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 rabbit (about 1.2 kg) and/or 1 partridge, cut in pieces
2 tortas de gazpacho (unleavened flatbreads, substitute thin water crackers), broken
steps: Brown the rabbit pieces in the oil in a deep pan over medium-high heat for 10 minutes; set aside.
Soften the onion, garlic and pepper for 8 minutes, add the tomato and cook 5 minutes.
Return the meat with water, thyme and bay leaf and simmer covered 40 minutes until tender and cooked through; remove bones if you wish.
Add the broken tortas, stir and simmer 5–8 minutes until they soften and thicken the stew; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g lean pork, in small dice
steps: Brown the pork in the oil in a cazuela over high heat for 6–8 minutes; add the chorizo for 2 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic and chilli and cook 8 minutes until soft.
Pour in the wine, then the tomato and salt, cover and simmer gently 30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the peas for the last 8 minutes and serve in small clay dishes with bread, Toledo-style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the panceta for 5 minutes until it renders and crisps.
Add the chorizo and fry 2–3 minutes until its red fat is released.
Beat the eggs with salt, pour into the pan and stir gently over low heat until softly scrambled and fully set, about 3 minutes.
Serve at once with bread, as Don Quixote ate on Saturdays.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 partridges, cleaned and trussed (substitute poussins or quail)
steps: Season the partridges and brown them in a heavy pot in 4 tbsp of the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes.
Add the onions, garlic, carrots, bay and peppercorns, then the rest of the oil, wine and vinegar and enough water to almost cover.
Cover and simmer gently 60 minutes until the birds are cooked through and tender.
Serve warm or cold in their lightly pickled (escabeche-style) liquor with the vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 rabbit and 1 partridge or 1 chicken thigh, in pieces
1 tsp ground cloves, cinnamon and caraway mixed
steps: Simmer the rabbit, partridge, liver and panceta in salted water for 1.5 hours until tender; strain, keeping the broth.
Remove all bones and mince or shred the meats finely.
In a pan fry the garlic in the lard, add the pimentón and spices, then the meats and breadcrumbs, stirring.
Add broth gradually and cook 20 minutes over low heat, stirring, until it forms a thick spreadable paste; top with pine nuts.
Serve warm on toasted bread, Cuenca-style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 dried ñora peppers (substitute 1 tsp sweet pimentón)
steps: Desalt the cod for 24–36 hours, changing water often, then grill it over embers or a hot pan until lightly charred and flake it.
Char the onions, garlic, peppers and tomatoes directly on embers or under a hot grill for 20 minutes until blackened (tiznado), then peel and cut in strips.
Lay potatoes in a clay pot with the vegetables, cod and ñoras, cover with water and the oil.
Simmer 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the fish is hot through; serve in the pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g Queso Manchego curado, cut in wedges 1 cm thick (use a vegetarian-rennet Manchego-style cheese for strict vegetarians)
steps: Remove the rind from the cheese and place the wedges in a clean glass jar with the herbs, garlic and peppercorns.
Cover completely with the olive oil, ensuring no cheese is exposed.
Seal and refrigerate for at least 3 days to infuse; use within 2 weeks.
Bring to room temperature for 30 minutes and serve as a tapa with bread, drizzling with some of the oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Gently heat the water, honey and 100 g of the icing sugar until dissolved, then remove from the heat.
Mix the almonds and remaining icing sugar, add the syrup and lemon juice and knead to a smooth, firm paste; rest in the fridge for 12 hours if possible.
Shape into small figures (figuritas) or crescents about 2 cm thick.
Brush the tops with a little syrup and grill or bake at 230°C for 3–5 minutes until just golden; cool before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml olive or sunflower oil, for frying
100 g honey or 6 tbsp sugar, to finish
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, flour, zest and salt into a smooth batter like cream.
Heat the oil to 180°C with the flower-shaped iron (molde de flores) submerged in it for 5 minutes.
Dip the hot iron into the batter up to but not over the rim, then plunge into the oil; shake gently to release and fry 1–2 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper and drizzle with honey or dust with sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 ml water and 150 g sugar for the syrup
100 ml sweet wine (vino dulce) or Málaga
steps: Whisk the whites stiff, beat in 150 g sugar, then fold in the yolks and the flour gently.
Spread in a lined tray 2–3 cm deep and bake at 180°C for 15–18 minutes until springy; cool and cut into rectangles.
Boil the water, sugar and cinnamon stick 5 minutes, cool slightly and add the sweet wine.
Place the sponges in paper cases, soak generously with the syrup until saturated and dust with cinnamon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat the honey in a pan over low heat until it bubbles and darkens slightly, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the almonds, breadcrumbs, zest and anise and cook 5 minutes until it forms a thick, sticky mass.
Spread it quickly between two wafer sheets per piece to a round 1 cm thick and press flat.
Leave to cool and harden for 1 hour before cutting into wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g fresh tocino (pork fat) and 1 ham bone
2 garlic cloves and 3 tbsp olive oil
steps: Put the beef, chicken, tocino and ham bone into a large pot with cold water, bring to the boil and skim well; add the drained chickpeas in a net bag.
Simmer very gently for 2.5 hours, adding hot water as needed, then add the carrots and potatoes for the final 30 minutes.
Separately boil the chorizos and morcilla for 20 minutes (so they don't stain the broth) and cook the cabbage, then sauté it with garlic and olive oil.
Strain off the broth and cook the fideos in it for 4 minutes for the first course (sopa).
Serve the vuelcos: chickpeas and vegetables as second course, then the sliced meats, with tomato sauce and pickled guindillas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef tripe (callos), cleaned and cut in squares
1 tbsp sweet pimentón and 1 tsp hot pimentón
steps: Scrub the tripe with salt and vinegar, rinse well, then blanch with the trotter in boiling water for 5 minutes and drain.
Cover with fresh water with half the onion, bay leaf and garlic and simmer 3 hours until very tender, adding the chorizo and morcilla in the last 30 minutes.
Bone the trotter and dice it; slice the sausages.
Fry the rest of the onion and jamón in the oil, add pimentóns and chilli off the heat, then stir into the pot with the meats and simmer 20 minutes more until thick and gelatinous.
Ideally rest overnight in the fridge and reheat thoroughly before serving in clay dishes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into thin chips
80 g jamón serrano, in thin slices
steps: Heat the oil in a deep pan to 160°C and fry the potatoes for 10–12 minutes until soft, then raise to 180°C for 3 minutes until golden; drain and salt.
Pile the chips on a hot plate and lay the jamón over them.
Fry the eggs in hot oil, basting, for 1–2 minutes until the whites are set and lacy at the edges.
Slide the eggs on top and break them at the table so the yolks run over the potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole sea bream (besugo), about 1.5 kg, cleaned and scaled (substitute red snapper)
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C, lay the potatoes in an oiled baking dish, season and bake 15 minutes.
Make 3 deep slashes in each side of the fish, insert lemon slices, season with salt and place on the potatoes.
Mix the garlic, parsley, breadcrumbs, lemon juice and wine with the oil and spoon over the fish.
Bake 20–25 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes at the bone; serve at once (a Madrid Christmas Eve classic).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g squid tubes, cleaned and cut in 1 cm rings
4 crusty barra rolls or baguette pieces
500 ml olive or sunflower oil, for frying
steps: Dry the squid rings thoroughly with paper towels and toss in flour and salt, shaking off excess.
Heat the oil to 185°C and fry the rings in batches for 1.5–2 minutes until pale golden and crisp; drain on paper.
Split the bread rolls and fill generously with the hot calamares.
Add a squeeze of lemon or a swipe of alioli and eat immediately, as around Plaza Mayor.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg lamb small intestines and mesentery (gallinejas and entresijos), thoroughly cleaned by the butcher
500 ml olive oil or lamb fat, for frying
steps: Rinse the gallinejas well in cold water, drain and dry thoroughly; season with salt.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170°C.
Fry the gallinejas in batches in their own released fat and oil for 12–15 minutes until crisp, deeply golden and cooked through.
Fry the chips in the same oil, drain everything on paper, and serve hot with lemon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Scrub the ears, singe off any hairs, and simmer in salted water with the onion and bay leaf for 1.5–2 hours until tender.
Drain, cool and cut into strips 1 cm wide.
Heat a griddle or frying pan with the oil over high heat and fry the ear strips with the garlic for 6–8 minutes until crisp and caramelised.
Sprinkle with both pimentóns and coarse salt and serve hot with a spicy brava sauce if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g salt cod loin, desalted and cut in strips 2 cm wide
1 pinch saffron, steeped in 1 tbsp warm water
steps: Desalt the cod for 24–36 hours in cold water in the fridge, changing water several times, then dry well.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, saffron water and sparkling water into a light batter.
Heat the oil to 180°C, dip each cod strip in batter and fry 3–4 minutes until golden and the fish is cooked through.
Drain and serve each "soldier" with a strip of red pepper draped across like a sash.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg live land snails (caracoles), purged and cleaned (or pre-cooked frozen snails)
1 tbsp sweet pimentón and 1 dried guindilla
steps: If using live snails, purge them for a day as instructed by the supplier, then wash repeatedly with salt and vinegar until no more slime remains.
Put them in cold water, bring slowly to the boil (so they emerge), skim, and simmer 1.5 hours until tender.
Fry the onion, garlic, chorizo and jamón in the oil for 10 minutes, add tomato, pimentón and guindilla and cook 10 minutes.
Add the drained snails with a little cooking water and simmer 20 minutes; serve in clay dishes with toothpicks and bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre olive or sunflower oil, for frying
steps: Pour the boiling salted water over the flour and baking powder and beat vigorously into a smooth, sticky dough; rest 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan to 185°C.
Pipe the dough through a large star nozzle into a long spiral in the oil, fry 3–4 minutes turning once until golden and crisp, then lift out.
Drain, cut into lengths with scissors and serve with thick hot chocolate for dipping, as in Madrid's chocolaterías.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Make the crema pastelera: heat the milk with cinnamon, whisk yolks, sugar and cornflour, pour over the milk and cook stirring until thick and bubbling for 1 minute; chill.
Knead the flour, olive oil, wine and salt to a smooth dough, rest 20 minutes and roll thin.
Cut into triangles, spoon cream onto each, fold over and seal the edges firmly with a fork.
Fry at 175°C for 2 minutes per side until golden, drain and dust with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 egg white and 150 g icing sugar for "listas" glaze
steps: Beat the eggs, sugar, oil and aniseed, then knead in the flour and baking powder to a soft dough.
Shape into small rings (rosquillas) about 7 cm across and place on a lined tray.
Bake at 180°C for 12–15 minutes until golden (these are the "tontas", plain).
For "listas", whisk the egg white, icing sugar and lemon juice to a thick glaze, brush over the cooled rings and dry in a 100°C oven for 5 minutes until set and white.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g day-old rustic bread (pan de pueblo), cut into small cubes
1 tsp sweet smoked pimentón de la Vera
steps: The night before, sprinkle the bread with the salted water, toss, cover with a damp cloth and leave overnight to soften.
Fry the garlic in olive oil in a wide pan, then add the panceta, chorizo and peppers and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes until the pork is cooked and crisp; remove them, leaving the fat.
Add the bread and pimentón and cook over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, turning and chopping constantly with a spatula, until loose, golden and crumbly.
Return the meats and peppers, toss and serve hot, traditionally with grapes or melon on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg lamb shoulder or kid goat, cut into pieces
2 roasted red peppers or 2 dried ñora peppers, soaked and scraped
1 tbsp sweet pimentón de la Vera

1 tbsp sweet pimentón de la Vera

Add the whole garlic cloves and bay and fry 3 minutes more.
Off the heat stir in both pimentones, then add the wine and a splash of water.

2 tbsp sweet pimentón de la Vera

Mix flour, olive oil, wine and salt into a smooth dough, rest 20 minutes and roll thinly; cut into 10 cm circles.

Fry in oil at 175°C for 2 minutes per side until golden, drain and dust with icing sugar; a Christmas sweet.

Line small greased tins with thin dough, crimp the edges into a star shape and fill with the cheese mixture.
Bake at 180°C for 40–50 minutes until golden and set; cool before serving.
